# hackbuild-motion

> hackbuild-motion is a set of ESM packages under @hackbuild for moving 3D characters on the web: springs and seeded noise, a humanoid bone mapper, inverse kinematics, procedural legged gait, clip retargeting with BVH and VMD readers, a runtime for a quadruped motion network, motion matching, gaze, blink and idle presence, avatar loading for VRM, GLB and FBX, a three.js stage host, lit scenes, lip sync, a GLB and clip baker, and Vue and custom element views. The cores are Rust compiled to wasm, three.js is a peer, model and weight files are never bundled and load from a URL or a file you give, and every package has a single file build that runs from file://.

Every package is ESM only with types included, installs from npm under @hackbuild, and is MIT. Each llms.md below lists the package's exports with signatures, minimal examples and the mistakes to avoid. Code: https://github.com/hackbuild/hackbuild-motion

## Packages

- [@hackbuild/avatar](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/avatar/llms.md): Load VRM, Mixamo, UAL, generic GLB, FBX and MMD characters into one humanoid space, with material repair, a wardrobe, expressions and a first person head hider.
- [@hackbuild/avatar-host](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/avatar-host/llms.md): Host a character on a three.js stage in any container, with a follow camera, the presence frame order and a loop that pauses when nobody can see it.
- [@hackbuild/bake](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/bake/llms.md): Optimize GLB models, bake animation clips into compact packs, and keep an asset lock with licences and hashes, in the browser, in Node or on the command line.
- [@hackbuild/environment](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/environment/llms.md): Light a three.js scene around a character with a key light, a rim light, image light and a set built from kit models.
- [@hackbuild/gait](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/gait/llms.md): Procedural locomotion for legged rigs: Froude gait choice, leg oscillators, footfall tables, posture springs, tail and ears, with a Rust core in wasm.
- [@hackbuild/ik](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/ik/llms.md): Inverse kinematics for characters on the web: two bone, FABRIK, CCD, clamped look at, finger curl and foot locking, with a Rust core in wasm.
- [@hackbuild/lipsync](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/lipsync/llms.md): Move a character's mouth from speech timings or the audio level, out to Oculus visemes, VRM vowels or ARKit blendshapes.
- [@hackbuild/motion-match](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/motion-match/llms.md): Motion matching over a clip database, with inertialized transitions, on a Rust core compiled to wasm.
- [@hackbuild/motion-net](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/motion-net/llms.md): Run the published quadruped categorical codebook matching network in the browser and drive a dog's gait from it.
- [@hackbuild/motion-views](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/motion-views/llms.md): Put a character stage, an avatar drop card and a clip strip on your page, drawn with the hackbuild-ui stylesheet, as custom elements or Vue components.
- [@hackbuild/organic](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/organic/llms.md): Critically damped springs, inertialization, seeded noise and samplers for procedural animation, with a Rust core in wasm.
- [@hackbuild/presence](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/presence/llms.md): Make a standing humanoid look present: gaze, blink, breath, idle moves, gestures, a layered clip player and a face driver.
- [@hackbuild/retarget](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/retarget/llms.md): Move clips between any rigs through one normalized humanoid space, with readers for BVH, VMD, VPD, VRMA and Unity text clips.
- [@hackbuild/rig](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/rig/llms.md): Bring any humanoid or legged skeleton into one normalized space: bone name mapping with no per rig table, limb chains, rest pose analysis, and the expression and viseme table.

# @hackbuild/avatar

> Load VRM, Mixamo, UAL, generic GLB, FBX and MMD characters into one humanoid space, with material repair, a wardrobe, expressions and a first person head hider.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/avatar/

## Purpose

- Loads a URL, bytes or a dropped file, sniffs the format from its content (GLB, glTF, VRM, VRMA, binary and ASCII FBX), and places the model in the normalized humanoid space: VRM 1.0 bone names, T pose, +Z forward, meters, feet at y = 0.
- Repairs materials that render wrong in three.js: Phong and Lambert to standard, cutouts for hair and lashes, black base colors under a texture, duplicate and failed maps.
- Finds the textures of a dropped folder by path, name, cleaned stem or key words, and fills missing color maps from the files you dropped.
- Sorts meshes into 17 wardrobe slots, drives expressions on any model through one `setValue(name, weight)`, and hides the head for a first person camera.
- Checks VRM licence metadata before an avatar goes into a shareable bundle.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/avatar three @pixiv/three-vrm
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/rig`, which maps bone names in wasm. three.js and the VRM and MMD loaders are optional peers behind their subpaths; install the ones you use.

| subpath | needs | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/avatar` | nothing; format sniffing, the FBX probe, wardrobe classifier, texture index and licence gate | none |
| `@hackbuild/avatar/three` | `three` (optional peer) | 0.186.1 or later |
| `@hackbuild/avatar/vrm` | `three` and `@pixiv/three-vrm` (optional peers) | three-vrm 3.5.5 or later |
| `@hackbuild/avatar/mmd` | `three`, `@pixiv/three-vrm` and `@moeru/three-mmd` (optional peers, three-mmd is a beta) | three-mmd 0.2.0-beta.3 or later |
| `@hackbuild/avatar/iife` | a page with a `THREE` global; leaves out `/vrm` and `/mmd` | none |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/avatar

```ts
function alternates(names: readonly string[]): Set<string>
```

Names that are alternates of another present name (`Shorts_down`, `Shorts_on_leg`, `No_stocking_L` beside `Shorts` and `stocking_L`).

```ts
type AvatarFormat = "vrm" | "vrma" | "glb" | "gltf" | "fbx" | "unknown"
```

The file format an avatar was sniffed as.

```ts
function categorize(name: string): Category | null
```

The best slot for a name, or null when no keyword scores.

```ts
interface Category {
  group: PartGroup;
  label: "neck" | "eyewear" | "headwear" | "hairAccessory" | "ear" | "hand" | "prop" | "outerwear" | "onepiece" | "top" | "bottom" | "legwear" | "footwear" | "underwear" | "hair" | "face" | "body";
  score: number;
}
```

The wardrobe slot a part name scores best for: group, label and score.

```ts
function checkRedistribution(meta: VrmMetaLike | null | undefined, opts: { modified: boolean }): RedistributionVerdict
```

Whether an avatar may go into a shareable bundle.

```ts
function cleanStem(p: string): string
```

File name with copy suffixes and the image extension removed, lowercase.

```ts
interface FbxProbe {
  deformer: boolean;
  geometry: boolean;
  kind: "unknown" | "character" | "clip";
}
```

What the first 256 KB of an FBX file say: a character, a clip or unknown, and whether it holds geometry and deformers.

```ts
function gltfJson(bytes: Uint8Array): Record<string, unknown> | null
```

glTF JSON from a GLB or a .gltf text file, or null.

```ts
const GROUP_ORDER: readonly PartGroup[]
```

Order for toggle lists: clothing first, base last.

```ts
function guessUnit(headOverFeet: number): number
```

Unit guess from head over feet height in source units: the first of meters, decimeters, centimeters, inches and millimeters that puts a head joint (about 87 percent of stature, inferred) at 1.0 to 2.3 m stature.

```ts
function hiddenInFile(bytes: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>): Set<string>
```

Model names the file marks invisible, from binary or ASCII FBX bytes.

```ts
type HumanBone = typeof HUMAN_BONES[number]
```

One VRM 1.0 humanoid bone name.

```ts
function load(source?: WasmSource): Promise<void>
```

Loads the wasm.

```ts
function loadSync(source: ArrayBuffer | Module | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>): void
```

Loads the wasm synchronously from bytes or a compiled module.

```ts
type PartGroup = "clothing" | "accessory" | "hair" | "base"
```

The wardrobe group of a part: clothing, accessory, hair or base.

```ts
function partLabel(raw: string): string
```

Strips exporter decoration: VRoid prefixes, "(Instance)", copy suffixes.

```ts
function probeFbx(bytes: Uint8Array): FbxProbe
```

Tells a rigged character from an animation only file by reading the first 256 KB: a character's Definitions section declares both Geometry and Deformer object types, a clip declares neither.

```ts
interface RedistributionVerdict {
  needsConfirm?: boolean;
  ok: boolean;
  reason?: string;
}
```

Whether an avatar may go into a shareable bundle, whether the user must confirm, and why not.

```ts
const SLOT_KEYWORDS: Record<SlotLabel, readonly string[]>
```

Keywords per slot, including the romanized Japanese names VRoid and Booth models use.

```ts
const SLOT_LABELS: readonly ["eyewear", "headwear", "hairAccessory", "neck", "ear", "hand", "prop", "outerwear", "onepiece", "top", "bottom", "legwear", "footwear", "underwear", "hair", "face", "body"]
```

Every wardrobe slot a part can be sorted into, accessories first and the base body last.

```ts
type SlotLabel = typeof SLOT_LABELS[number]
```

One wardrobe slot name from `SLOT_LABELS`.

```ts
function sniffFormat(bytes: Uint8Array, name?: string): AvatarFormat
```

Format from content; the file name breaks no ties, it only helps when the content says nothing.

```ts
const SPHERE_MAP: RegExp
```

MMD sphere maps: a lighting lookup, never a surface color.

```ts
class TextureIndex {
  constructor(files: readonly string[], modelName?: string);
  readonly files: string[];
  forReference(ref: string): string | null;
  key(stem: string): string;
  match(ref: string): TextureMatch | null;
}
```

Finds the dropped image file a model's texture reference means, by exact path, file name, cleaned stem or key words.

```ts
interface TextureMatch {
  file: string;
  score: number;
}
```

One candidate file for a texture reference and how well it matched.

```ts
function tokens(name: string): string[]
```

Lowercase word tokens: camelCase, snake, kebab, dots and digits split.

```ts
interface VrmMetaLike {
  allowRedistribution?: boolean;
  licenseName?: string;
  metaVersion?: string;
  modification?: string;
  otherLicenseUrl?: string;
}
```

VRM 1.0 and 0.x metadata fields the gate reads.

### @hackbuild/avatar/mmd

```ts
function buildSprings(model: MmdModelData, bones: readonly Bone<Object3DEventMap>[], humanoid: ReadonlySet<Object3D<Object3DEventMap>>, unit: number): VRMSpringBoneManager | null
```

MMD rigid bodies as three-vrm spring bones.

```ts
function loadMmd(src: MmdSource, opts?: MmdLoadOptions): Promise<MmdAvatar>
```

Loads a dropped PMX or PMD model into the normalized humanoid space and wraps it as a VRM: `avatar.vrm.vrm` is the three-vrm `VRM`, its normalized bones are `avatar.bones`, and `avatar.update(dt)` steps expressions, gaze and springs.

```ts
const MMD_LOCAL_COPY: "mmd models usually forbid sharing. this one stays on this device."
```

The readme limits of most MMD models, said once on load.

```ts
const MMD_UNIT: 0.08
```

Meters per MMD unit (vendor, the MMD convention of 8 cm).

```ts
interface MmdAvatar extends Avatar {
  animations: AnimationClip[];
  bones: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>;
  dialect: string;
  expressions: ExpressionSink & Partial<Pick<ExpressionRig, "apply" | "reset" | "found">>;
  format: "unknown";
  head: HeadHider | null;
  humanoid: Humanoid | null;
  local: true;
  physics: { colliders: number; joints: number };
  repair: RepairReport | null;
  root: Object3D;
  vrm: VrmResult;
  wardrobe: Wardrobe;
  warnings: string[];
  dispose(): void;
  update(dt: number): void;
}
```

An MMD model loaded as an avatar, with its VRM result and the spring physics built from its rigid bodies.

```ts
function mmdFormat(bytes: Uint8Array): "pmx" | "pmd" | null
```

"pmx" or "pmd" from the first bytes, else null.

```ts
interface MmdLoaderLike {
  loadAsync(url: string): Promise<{ mesh: SkinnedMesh; pmx: MmdModelData }>;
  setResourcePath(path: string): unknown;
}
```

The part of three-mmd's MMDLoader this module calls.

```ts
interface MmdLoadOptions {
  files?: FileTextures;
  manager?: LoadingManager;
  name?: string;
  normalize?: Omit<NormalizeOptions, "unit" | "deform">;
  parser?: () => Promise<{ MMDLoader: new (manager?: LoadingManager) => MmdLoaderLike }>;
  springs?: boolean;
  unit?: number;
}
```

Name, dropped textures, loading manager, unit and physics options of `loadMmd`.

```ts
interface MmdModelData {
  bones: readonly { position: Vec3 }[];
  rigidBodies: readonly MmdRigidBody[];
}
```

The parts of a parsed PMX model the spring builder reads.

```ts
interface MmdRigidBody {
  boneIndex: number;
  linearDamping: number;
  name?: string;
  physicsMode: number;
  shapePosition: Vec3;
  shapeRotation: Vec3;
  shapeSize: Vec3;
  shapeType: number;
}
```

The parts of a parsed PMX rigid body the spring builder reads.

```ts
type MmdSource = Blob | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | string | URL
```

What `loadMmd` reads: a file, bytes or a URL.

```ts
function spineUnderHips(bones: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>): boolean
```

MMD hangs the upper and lower body side by side under the center bone; a VRM spine grows out of its hips.

```ts
function springSettings(boneName: string, linearDamping: number, sizeX: number, unit: number): { dragForce: number; gravityDir: Vector3; gravityPower: number; hitRadius: number; stiffness: number }
```

Joint settings for a simulated bone: skirts a little stiffer than hair and ribbons (vendor).

### @hackbuild/avatar/three

```ts
function applyStartingVisibility(root: Object3D, hidden: ReadonlySet<string>): number
```

Hides the meshes an FBX file stores switched off (`hiddenInFile`), before the wardrobe reads visibility.

```ts
interface Avatar {
  animations: AnimationClip[];
  bones: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>;
  dialect: string;
  expressions: ExpressionSink & Partial<Pick<ExpressionRig, "apply" | "reset" | "found">>;
  format: AvatarFormat;
  head: HeadHider | null;
  humanoid: Humanoid | null;
  repair: RepairReport | null;
  root: Object3D;
  vrm: VrmResult | null;
  wardrobe: Wardrobe;
  warnings: string[];
  dispose(): void;
  update(dt: number): void;
}
```

A loaded character in the normalized humanoid space: root, bones, wardrobe, expressions, clips and metadata.

```ts
type AvatarSource = string | URL | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | Blob
```

What `loadAvatar` reads: a URL, bytes or a file.

```ts
function bakeScale(root: Object3D, s: number): void
```

Scales `root` and everything under it by `s` in place; the root keeps scale 1.

```ts
function coverage(img: ImageSample, uvs: Float32Array): number
```

Share of UV centers on painted pixels.

```ts
function disposeObject(root: Object3D): void
```

Frees every geometry, material, texture and skeleton under `root` and detaches it.

```ts
class ExpressionRig {
  constructor(root: Object3D);
  readonly found: Partial<Record<VrmExpression, ResolvedExpression>>;
  readonly morphNames: string[];
  apply(): void;
  getValue(name: string): number;
  reset(): void;
  setValue(name: string, weight: number): void;
}
```

VRM presets on a plain model through the rig expression table: each preset resolves once to morphs, and every mesh that carries a morph name joins, so a face split from its lashes blinks as one.

```ts
interface ExpressionSink {
  setValue(name: string, weight: number): void;
}
```

What a face driver writes to: a preset or morph name and a weight.

```ts
interface FileTextures {
  index: TextureIndex;
  manager: LoadingManager;
  misses: string[];
  dispose(): void;
  texture(file: string): Texture;
}
```

A loading manager over dropped files that resolves texture references through a `TextureIndex`, with the references it could not match.

```ts
function fillMaps(root: Object3D, files: Pick<FileTextures, "index" | "texture">, report: RepairReport): Promise<void>
```

Drops color maps that failed and fills missing ones from the dropped files: the material's UV tile, then its name, then a sibling's image that covers its UVs (see `pickMaps`).

```ts
class HeadHider {
  constructor(head: Object3D, scale?: number);
  readonly head: Object3D;
  readonly scale: number;
  during<T>(draw: () => T): T;
  hide(): void;
  render(renderer: { render(scene: Scene, camera: Camera): void }, scene: Scene, camera: Camera): void;
  restore(): void;
}
```

Hides the head for a first person render by scaling the head bone to 0.001 for that render only, then restores it.

```ts
interface Humanoid {
  bones: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>;
  headHeight: number;
  model: Object3D;
  report: RigMapReport;
  rest: RestReport;
  root: Group;
}
```

A model placed in the normalized humanoid space: its root group, mapped bones, rig and rest reports and head height.

```ts
interface ImageSample {
  background: [number, number, number];
  pixels: Uint8ClampedArray;
  size: number;
}
```

A small copy of an image and its background color (the commonest color along its border).

```ts
function loadAvatar(src: AvatarSource, opts?: LoadOptions): Promise<Avatar>
```

Loads a character from a URL, bytes or a dropped File: VRM through the `/vrm` hook when given, glTF and GLB (Mixamo, UAL, generic) and FBX through the three.js loaders.

```ts
interface LoadOptions {
  files?: FileTextures;
  manager?: LoadingManager;
  name?: string;
  normalize?: NormalizeOptions;
  path?: string;
  repair?: false | RepairOptions;
  vrm?: VrmHook;
}
```

Name, resource path, manager, dropped textures, VRM hook, repair and normalize options of `loadAvatar`.

```ts
function managerForFiles(files: ReadonlyMap<string, string | Blob>, modelName?: string): FileTextures
```

A LoadingManager that sends every texture reference through a lenient index of the files the person dropped, so wrong paths in the model still find their images.

```ts
interface MapSources {
  byName(name: string): string | null;
  own(m: Material): string | null;
  sample(file: string): Promise<ImageSample | null>;
}
```

Where `pickMap` looks for a material's color map: its own map, a file named like it, and image samples.

```ts
type MapVia = "tile" | "name" | "coverage"
```

The rule that picked a color map: UV tile, material name or coverage.

```ts
function normalizeHumanoid(model: Object3D, opts?: NormalizeOptions): Humanoid
```

Maps the model's bones to VRM 1.0 names, bakes its units into the model (`bakeScale`, so spring bones see an unscaled root), then wraps it so it faces +Z, stands in meters with its feet on y = 0, and lifts A pose arms into the T pose.

```ts
interface NormalizeOptions {
  deform?: boolean;
  headHeight?: number;
  straightLegs?: boolean;
  tPoseArms?: boolean;
  unit?: number;
}
```

Head height, T pose arms, straight legs and unit options for placing a model in the normalized humanoid space.

```ts
interface Part {
  group: PartGroup | "other";
  id: string;
  label: "neck" | "eyewear" | "headwear" | "hairAccessory" | "ear" | "hand" | "prop" | "outerwear" | "onepiece" | "top" | "bottom" | "legwear" | "footwear" | "underwear" | "hair" | "face" | "body" | null;
  material?: Material<MaterialEventMap>;
  meshes: Mesh<BufferGeometry<NormalBufferAttributes, BufferGeometryEventMap>, Material<MaterialEventMap> | Material<MaterialEventMap>[], Object3DEventMap>[];
  name: string;
  visible: boolean;
}
```

One wardrobe part: its slot, group, meshes and, for a merged mesh, its material.

```ts
interface PickedMap {
  file: string;
  via: MapVia;
}
```

The image file chosen for a material and the rule that chose it.

```ts
function pickMaps(meshes: readonly Mesh<BufferGeometry<NormalBufferAttributes, BufferGeometryEventMap>, Material<MaterialEventMap> | Material<MaterialEventMap>[], Object3DEventMap>[], src: MapSources): Promise<Map<Material<MaterialEventMap>, PickedMap | null>>
```

A color map for every material on `meshes` with no own map: its tile's file, then its name match, then a sibling's image at coverage 0.6 or more.

```ts
function posedBounds(bones: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>, margin?: number): Box3
```

World bounds of the posed skeleton plus a margin, for camera framing; skinned bounds stay at rest size.

```ts
function readyOf(t: Texture<unknown, TextureEventMap> | null | undefined): Promise<boolean>
```

Settles true once a texture's image arrived, false when it failed or no file was found.

```ts
function repairMaterials(root: Object3D, opts?: RepairOptions): RepairReport
```

Fixes the exporter errors that make dropped models look wrong: Phong and Lambert become MeshStandardMaterial; an opaque material flagged transparent becomes a cutout (teeth and eye sorting); zero opacity over a texture becomes a cutout (Blender alpha setup); black base color under a texture becomes white; an alpha map that repeats the color map is dropped (FBXLoader reads it from the green channel); failed maps are dropped; color maps are sRGB; skinned meshes are never frustum culled, since their bounds stay at the rest pose.

```ts
interface RepairOptions {
  cutoff?: number;
  doubleSided?: boolean | (mesh: Mesh) => boolean;
  isBroken?: (t: Texture) => boolean;
}
```

Alpha cutoff, double sided faces and the broken texture test of the material repair.

```ts
interface RepairReport {
  byCoverage: number;
  byName: number;
  byTile: number;
  colorSpace: number;
  converted: number;
  cutouts: number;
  droppedMaps: number;
  misses: string[];
  whitened: number;
}
```

What the material repair changed, counted per kind.

```ts
function resolveTiles<M>(groups: readonly TileGroup<M>[], matched: (m: M) => string | null): Map<M, string | null>
```

The file each tiled group should show, given what its material matched by name (null for none).

```ts
function roughnessFromShininess(n: number): number
```

Blinn-Phong shininess to a roughness: sqrt(2 / (n + 2)), the usual Beckmann correspondence (inferred), clamped to 0.15 to 1.

```ts
const SAMPLE_SIZE: 128
```

Side of the copy an image is sampled from, pixels.

```ts
function sampleImage(image: Blob | HTMLImageElement | SVGImageElement | HTMLVideoElement | HTMLCanvasElement | ImageBitmap | OffscreenCanvas | VideoFrame | ImageData): Promise<ImageSample | null>
```

Samples a loaded image.

```ts
function samplePixels(pixels: Uint8ClampedArray, size?: number): ImageSample
```

An ImageSample from RGBA pixels of a `size` by `size` copy.

```ts
const SIBLING_MIN: 0.6
```

Least coverage for a sibling's image to be taken (vendor).

```ts
interface TileGroup<M> {
  material: M;
  tile: string | null;
  weight: number;
}
```

A material's share of a mesh: the UV tile it lies in and how many vertices use it.

```ts
function tileGroups(mesh: Mesh): TileGroup<Material<MaterialEventMap>>[]
```

Material groups of one mesh with the UV tile each lies in.

```ts
function uvCenters(mesh: Mesh, material: Material): Float32Array
```

UV centers of the material's triangles on `mesh`, wrapped to 0 to 1 (tiles and repeat wrapping sample one image).

```ts
interface VrmHook {
  finish(gltf: GLTF): VrmResult | null;
  register(loader: GLTFLoader): void;
}
```

What `/vrm` hands to `loadAvatar` so VRM files load through @pixiv/three-vrm.

```ts
interface VrmResult {
  bones: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>;
  expressions: ExpressionSink;
  meta: unknown;
  root: Object3D;
  vrm: unknown;
  update(dt: number): void;
}
```

A VRM as the loader hands it back: root, bones, expressions, the per frame update and the VRM metadata.

```ts
class Wardrobe {
  constructor();
  readonly parts: Part[];
  equip(id: string): void;
  get(id: string): Part | undefined;
  restore(s: Record<string, boolean>): void;
  setVisible(id: string, on: boolean): void;
  slot(label: "neck" | "eyewear" | "headwear" | "hairAccessory" | "ear" | "hand" | "prop" | "outerwear" | "onepiece" | "top" | "bottom" | "legwear" | "footwear" | "underwear" | "hair" | "face" | "body"): Part[];
  snapshot(): Record<string, boolean>;
  toggle(id: string): boolean;
  static from(root: Object3D): Wardrobe;
}
```

Parts per mesh, or per material when one mesh carries several named materials (merged MMD style meshes).

### @hackbuild/avatar/vrm

```ts
const EYE_RANGE: { readonly pitch: 8; readonly yaw: 12 }
```

Eye turn limits for non VRM eye bones, degrees: sideways 12, up and down 8 (vendor).

```ts
function fromVrm(vrm: VRM, opts?: VrmHookOptions): VrmResult
```

Builds the result `loadAvatar` returns for a VRM.

```ts
function toVrm(avatar: Pick<Avatar, "root" | "bones" | "vrm">, opts?: ToVrmOptions): VRM
```

Wraps a loaded non VRM avatar (GLB, FBX) in an in memory three-vrm `VRM`, so one frame loop drives every format: a humanoid whose normalized bones have identity rest rotations, an expression manager built from the rig expression table, eye bone look at inside `EYE_RANGE`, and optional springs.

```ts
interface ToVrmOptions {
  name?: string;
  springs?(root: Object3D): VRMSpringBoneManager | null;
}
```

Spring bones and meta name for turning a loaded avatar into a VRM.

```ts
function vrmBones(vrm: VRM): Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>
```

Normalized bones of a loaded VRM by VRM 1.0 name.

```ts
function vrmExpressionSink(vrm: VRM): ExpressionSink
```

The VRM expression manager as a sink; unknown names are ignored by three-vrm.

```ts
function vrmHook(opts?: VrmHookOptions): VrmHook
```

Pass as `loadAvatar(src, { vrm: vrmHook() })`.

```ts
interface VrmHookOptions {
  combineSkeletons?: boolean;
  removeUnusedVertices?: boolean;
}
```

Vertex cleanup and skeleton merge options of the VRM loader hook.

```ts
function vrmMeta(vrm: VRM): VrmMetaLike
```

Metadata in the shape `checkRedistribution` reads.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { load } from "@hackbuild/avatar";
import { loadAvatar } from "@hackbuild/avatar/three";
import { vrmHook } from "@hackbuild/avatar/vrm";
import * as THREE from "three";

await load(); // the rig wasm that maps bone names
const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer();
renderer.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight);
const scene = new THREE.Scene().add(new THREE.HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x444444, 2.5));
const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(30, innerWidth / innerHeight, 0.05, 50);
camera.position.set(0, 1.4, 3.2);
const input = Object.assign(document.createElement("input"), { type: "file", accept: ".vrm,.glb,.gltf,.fbx" });
document.body.append(input, renderer.domElement);

// you pick the model file; it keeps its own licence
input.onchange = async () => {
  const file = input.files?.[0];
  if (!file) return;
  const avatar = await loadAvatar(file, { name: file.name, vrm: vrmHook() });
  console.log(avatar.format, avatar.dialect, avatar.warnings);
  scene.add(avatar.root);
  renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => (avatar.update(1 / 60), renderer.render(scene, camera)));
};
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const files = new Map([...dropped].map((f) => [f.webkitRelativePath || f.name, f] as const));
const avatar = await loadAvatar(model, { name: model.name, files: managerForFiles(files, "model") });
console.log(avatar.repair?.misses); // references no dropped file matched
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Loading a `.vrm` without `vrm: vrmHook()`: it loads as plain glTF with no spring bones or expressions.
- Forgetting `await load()` before `loadAvatar`: the rig wasm maps the bones.
- Adding `avatar.humanoid.model` or the raw glTF scene to your scene instead of `avatar.root`, which holds the normalized wrapper.
- Sharing or bundling a model without `checkRedistribution`, or uploading an MMD model the result marks `local: true`.
- Using skinned mesh bounds for framing: they stay at the rest pose. Use `posedBounds(avatar.bones)`.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/rig: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (bone mapping ran before the rig wasm loaded): `await load()` from `@hackbuild/avatar` first
- `avatar: missing required bones: <bones>.` (the mapper found no hips, spine, arms or legs): check the file is a rigged humanoid; a prop or clip only file has no skeleton
- `avatar: rest analysis needs hips, head and both arms.` (the rest pose could not be measured): use a full humanoid rig
- `avatar: a vrma file is an animation. load it with a clip loader.` (a VRMA was passed to `loadAvatar`): load it as a clip with `@hackbuild/retarget`
- `avatar: unknown model format.` (the bytes and the name match no format): pass `name` with the extension, or check the file
- `avatar: fetch failed with <status> for <url>.` (the URL answered with an error): check the URL and that the server allows the page's origin
- `avatar: no humanoid skeleton, missing <bones>.` (`toVrm` found too few normalized bones): load the model through `loadAvatar` first and check `avatar.bones`
- `avatar: the mmd file did not parse. <reason>` (three-mmd could not read the PMX or PMD): check the file and drop its folder so textures resolve

---

# @hackbuild/avatar-host

> Host a character on a three.js stage in any container, with a follow camera, the presence frame order and a loop that pauses when nobody can see it.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/avatar-host/

## Purpose

- Gives you a stage in any element: a renderer sized to its container, orbit controls, plain lights or a lit scene, and a `hb-avatar-host` custom element for pages with no framework.
- Loads bodies through `@hackbuild/avatar` with ticketed loads, so a slow load that a newer one overtook is freed and never shown.
- Runs one frame order for every body: clip player, head level, pose, gaze, face with lid and mouth, then the avatar update.
- Frames the posed body with a camera that eases, holds still inside a dead zone and leaves a hand zoom alone.
- Stops the loop while the page is hidden, the stage is off screen, inactive or covered, or the 3D context is lost, and draws previews of clips and avatars in the background.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/avatar-host @hackbuild/avatar three @pixiv/three-vrm
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/avatar`, `@hackbuild/presence`, `@hackbuild/lipsync`, `@hackbuild/environment`, `@hackbuild/organic` and `@hackbuild/rig`, which install with it. `three` is an optional peer needed by `/three` and `/thumbs`. `@pixiv/three-vrm` is needed only to show VRM files, and is imported on the first `.vrm` through the hook you pass.

| subpath | needs | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/avatar-host` | nothing; the ticketed host, drop sources, the stage loop and failure copy | none |
| `@hackbuild/avatar-host/three` | `three` (optional peer), WebGL | 0.186.1 or later |
| `@hackbuild/avatar-host/thumbs` | `three`, WebGL | 0.186.1 or later |
| `@hackbuild/avatar-host/iife` | a page with a `THREE` global; leaves out three-vrm | none |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/avatar-host

```ts
interface Adapter<S extends HostSource, T, R = unknown> {
  key?: string;
  create(): Promise<R>;
  destroy?(runtime: R): void;
  load(runtime: R, source: S): Promise<T>;
}
```

Loads one kind of source: makes a runtime once, loads sources into it, and may destroy it.

```ts
class AvatarHost<S extends HostSource, T> {
  constructor(opts: AvatarHostOptions<S, T>);
  readonly current: T | null;
  readonly runtimes: string[];
  destroy(): void;
  show(source: S | Promise<S>): Promise<T | null>;
}
```

Shows one source at a time through adapters: each show takes a ticket, a load that a later show overtook is discarded, and runtimes are shared or destroyed by key.

```ts
interface AvatarHostOptions<S extends HostSource, T> {

  exclusive?: boolean;
  discard?(result: T): void;
}
```

The adapters by kind, the exclusive switch and the discard call of an `AvatarHost`.

### @hackbuild/avatar-host/thumbs

```ts
}
```

Image size, canvas and body load options of avatar previews.

```ts
interface AvatarThumbJob {
  id: string;
  source: BodySource;
}
```

One avatar to preview.

```ts
type AvatarThumbOptions = Omit<ThumbQueueOptions<AvatarThumbJob>, "renderer"> & { portrait?: AvatarPortraitOptions }
```

Queue and portrait options of `avatarThumbs`.

```ts
function avatarThumbs(opts: AvatarThumbOptions): ThumbQueue<AvatarThumbJob>
```

A queue of avatar previews, 240 by 320 px by default.

```ts
class ClipPortrait {
  readonly figure: Avatar;
  readonly lost: boolean;
  dispose(): void;
  draw(job: ClipThumbJob): Promise<Blob | null>;
  static create(opts?: ClipPortraitOptions): Promise<ClipPortrait>;
}
```

Clip previews on one clay figure.

```ts
interface ClipPortraitOptions extends PortraitOptions {
  canvas?: HTMLCanvasElement;
  color?: string | number;
  figure?: () => Avatar | Promise<Avatar>;
  height?: number;
  width?: number;
}
```

Image size, clay colour and figure of clip previews.

```ts
interface ClipThumbJob {
  hold?: boolean;
  id: string;
  clip(): AnimationClip | Promise<AnimationClip>;
}
```

One clip to preview: its id, the clip in normalized bone names, and whether it is a held pose.

Queue and portrait options of `clipThumbs`.

A queue of clip previews on one clay figure, 192 px square by default.

Points an orthographic camera at `box` from the portrait angle and fits it, `aspect` width over height.

```ts

```

Bones that judge a frame; fingers would outvote them by count.

```ts
  canvas?: HTMLCanvasElement;
  height?: number;
  width?: number;
}
```

Image width, height and canvas of a preview.

```ts

```

Frames tried when looking for the most telling one.

```ts
function tellingTime(figure: Avatar, clip: AnimationClip, hold?: boolean, samples?: number): number
```

The time of the clip's most telling frame on `figure`: for a held pose or a clip under 0.05 s its end, else the sampled frame between 10 and 90 percent whose measured bones turn furthest from their rest rotation (the ends are where most clips stand near rest).

```ts
interface ThumbProgress {
  active: boolean;
  done: number;
  total: number;
}
```

Counts for a progress line: items done of items asked for in this run.

```ts
class ThumbQueue<J extends { id: string }> {
  constructor(opts: ThumbQueueOptions<J>);
  readonly holding: boolean;
  readonly progress: ThumbProgress;
  readonly waiting: string[];
  destroy(): void;
  idle(): Promise<void>;
  want(jobs: readonly J[], urgent?: boolean): void;
}
```

Draws previews one at a time in the background, saves each image and remembers failures, paced so the page stays responsive.

```ts
interface ThumbQueueOptions<J> {
  lingerMs?: number;
  maxRestMs?: number;
  minRestMs?: number;
  failed?(id: string, reason: string): void;
  hidden?(): boolean;
  now?(): number;
  onProgress?(p: ThumbProgress): void;
  renderer(): Promise<ThumbRenderer<J> | null>;
  save(id: string, image: Blob): Promise<void>;
}
```

The renderer factory, the save call, the failure and progress calls of a `ThumbQueue`.

```ts
interface ThumbRenderer<J> {
  readonly lost: boolean;
  dispose(): void;
  draw(job: J): Promise<Blob | null>;
}
```

Draws one item to an image.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { AvatarStage } from "@hackbuild/avatar-host/three";

// the stage sizes itself to its container and pauses while hidden or off screen
const box = Object.assign(document.createElement("div"), { style: "height: 70vh" });
const input = Object.assign(document.createElement("input"), { type: "file", multiple: true });
document.body.append(input, box);
const stage = new AvatarStage(box, {
  // three-vrm is imported on the first .vrm only
  vrm: () => import("@hackbuild/avatar/vrm").then((m) => m.vrmHook()),
});
stage.on("failed", (e) => console.warn(e.message));
stage.on("stats", (e) => console.log(e.stats.fps.toFixed(0), "fps"));

// the placeholder body is built in code; pick a .vrm, .glb or .fbx (and its textures) to swap it
stage.showPlaceholder().setExpression("happy", 0.5);
input.onchange = async () => {
  const body = await stage.show([...(input.files ?? [])]);
  body?.setGazeMode("listen");
};
```

### from the concepts

```ts
stage.setActive(routeIsShown);
stage.setCovered(sheetOpen);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const body = stage.showPlaceholder();
body.play(waveClip, { layer: "upper" });
body.lip.push(speechEvents); // timed words or visemes from a speech engine
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Sizing the canvas to the window or calling `renderer.setSize` yourself: the stage follows its container.
- Leaving the loop running under a sheet or on a hidden route: call `setCovered` and `setActive`, or set the `covered` and `inactive` attributes.
- Writing bones or expression weights outside the body's frame order: use `body.play`, `body.setExpression` and `body.lip` so one owner writes each channel.
- Showing a VRM without the `vrm` hook in the stage options: it loads as plain glTF with no expressions or spring bones.
- Forgetting `stage.dispose()` when the stage leaves the page: it frees the body and the WebGL context.

## Errors this package throws

- `this file is a pmx. open it with the mmd loader of the avatar package.` (`sourceFromFiles` got a PMX or PMD): load it with `loadMmd` from `@hackbuild/avatar/mmd`, then `stage.showAvatar`
- `a <ext> file is an animation. drop a body: a .vrm, .glb, .gltf or .fbx.` (the drop held only a clip file): drop a model file
- `this drop has no model. drop a .vrm, .glb, .gltf or .fbx file.` (no model file in the drop): drop a model file
- `no adapter for <kind> files.` (`AvatarHost.show` got a kind with no adapter): add an adapter for that kind
- `this clip has <n> bones and the body <m>. build it with clipOf or over body.names.` (`body.play` got a clip built over another bone list): build the clip with `body.clipOf`
- `the clip moves no bone of this figure.` (a clip preview had no track for the figure's bones): check the clip's bone names; it reaches `failed(id, reason)`

---

# @hackbuild/bake

> Optimize GLB models, bake animation clips into compact packs, and keep an asset lock with licences and hashes, in the browser, in Node or on the command line.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/bake/

## Purpose

- Welds, simplifies and reorders the triangle meshes of a GLB, drops unused data, and hands each embedded image to your resize hook.
- Bakes clips of local rotations and a root track into an HBCP pack of int16 values, with a report of the quantization error, the loop seam and the foot contacts of each clip.
- Reads packs and samples clips in plain TypeScript, so a runtime reader needs no wasm.
- Writes and checks `assets.lock.json`: path, source, licence, SHA-256, size and an optional byte budget per asset.
- Gives the same bytes in a page, in Node and from the `hackbuild-bake` command line tool, which build from one Rust core.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/bake
```

No dependencies and no peers. Image decoding and resizing stay on your side, through the hook.

| subpath | what |
|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/bake` | optimize, clip bake, pack reader, lock |
| `@hackbuild/bake/wasm` | the wasm file, to pass to `load()` as a URL |
| `@hackbuild/bake/inline` | the wasm as base64 |
| `@hackbuild/bake/iife` | the single file build, global `HackbuildBake`, wasm inlined |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/bake

```ts
interface AssetEntry {
  budget?: number;
  bytes: number;
  licence: string;
  path: string;
  sha256: string;
  source: string;
}
```

One row of assets.lock.json: path, source, licence, SHA-256, bytes and an optional budget.

```ts
function bakeClips(input: BakeInput): { bytes: Uint8Array; pack: ClipPack; report: ClipReport[] }
```

Bakes clips into the compact HBCP pack and reports error, seams and contacts per clip.

```ts
interface BakeInput {
  clips: SourceClip[];
  contacts?: ContactRule;
  fps: number;
  seamLimitDeg?: number;
  skeleton: Skeleton;
}
```

Everything `bakeClips` takes: frame rate, skeleton, clips, contact rule and seam limit.

```ts
function checkLock(lockText: string, files: Map<string, Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>> | Record<string, Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>>, forbid?: string[]): { failures: string[]; ok: boolean }
```

Checks files against assets.lock.json: hashes, sizes, budgets, missing licences and licences matching a forbidden substring such as "NC".

```ts
interface ClipPack {
  clips: Record<string, PackedClip>;
  feet: string[];
  fps: number;
  parents: number[];
  roles: string[];
}
```

A decoded clip pack: frame rate, roles, parents, feet and clips by name.

```ts
interface ClipReport {
  contactFrames: number[];
  frames: number;
  largestStepDeg: number | null;
  maxAngleErrorDeg: number;
  maxPositionErrorM: number;
  name: string;
  seamAngleDeg: number | null;
  seamOk: boolean | null;
  worstFrame: number;
  worstRole: string;
}
```

Quantization error, seam and contacts of one baked clip.

```ts
interface ContactRule {
  feet: string[];
  height: number;
  minFrames: number;
  speed: number;
}
```

How foot contacts are found: foot roles, height and speed limits and the shortest contact.

```ts
function decodePack(buf: ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>): ClipPack
```

Reads the HBCP pack format; no wasm needed.

```ts
function goldenTrace(seed: number): Float64Array
```

A deterministic trace of the core for one seed, compared between the native and wasm builds in tests.

```ts
function listTextures(glb: ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>): TextureInfo[]
```

Lists the embedded images of a GLB with their roles and sizes.

```ts
function load(source?: WasmSource): Promise<void>
```

Loads the wasm core once: from a URL, bytes or a compiled module, or from the inlined copy when you pass nothing.

```ts
function loadSync(source: ArrayBuffer | Module | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>): void
```

Loads the wasm core synchronously from bytes or a compiled module.

```ts
function lockEntry(path: string, bytes: ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>, source: string, licence: string, budget?: number): AssetEntry
```

A lock row for one file, with its SHA-256 and byte count measured from the bytes.

```ts
function optimizeModel(glb: ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>, opts?: OptimizeOptions): Promise<{ glb: Uint8Array; report: OptimizeReport }>
```

Welds, simplifies and repacks a GLB, swapping in the images your resize hook returns.

```ts
interface OptimizeOptions {
  error?: number;
  lockBorder?: boolean;
  ratio?: number;
  resize?: TextureHook;
  textures?: Partial<Record<TextureRole, number>>;
}
```

Options of `optimizeModel`: simplification, texture limits and the resize hook.

```ts
interface OptimizeReport {
  bytesIn: number;
  bytesOut: number;
  primitives: number;
  skipped: string[];
  textures: { bytesIn: number; bytesOut: number; image: number; mime: string; role: TextureRole }[];
  trianglesIn: number;
  trianglesOut: number;
  verticesIn: number;
  verticesOut: number;
}
```

What `optimizeModel` changed: bytes, vertices, triangles, textures and skipped primitives.

```ts
interface PackedClip {
  contacts: Uint8Array;
  dur: number;
  loop: boolean;
  n: number;
  name: string;
  p: Int16Array;
  posScale: number;
  q: Int16Array;
}
```

One clip in a pack: int16 rotations and root positions and a contact byte per frame.

```ts
function sampleClip(pack: ClipPack, clip: PackedClip, t: number, out: Float32Array): [number, number, number]
```

Samples a packed clip at time `t` seconds into `out` (roles times 4 quaternion components) with normalized linear blending between frames.

```ts
function sha256Hex(bytes: ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>): string
```

The SHA-256 of bytes as lowercase hex, computed in the wasm core.

```ts
interface Skeleton {
  parents: number[];
  rest: [number, number, number][];
  roles: string[];
}
```

The rig of a clip set: role names, parents and rest translations.

```ts
interface SourceClip {
  loop?: boolean;
  name: string;
  p?: ArrayLike<number>;
  q: ArrayLike<number>;
}
```

One clip to bake: name, loop flag, local rotations and optional root translation.

```ts
function syntheticClips(seed: number): BakeInput
```

A walk loop, a broken loop and a one shot on an eight role leg rig.

```ts
function syntheticGlb(seed: number, grid: number): Uint8Array
```

A bumpy unindexed grid GLB with a line mesh and a fake 2048 px PNG.

```ts
type TextureHook = (t: TextureRequest) => Promise<{ bytes: Uint8Array; mime: string } | null> | { bytes: Uint8Array; mime: string } | null
```

Returns new bytes and their mime type, or null to keep the image.

```ts
interface TextureInfo {
  bytes: number;
  height: number | null;
  image: number;
  mime: string;
  role: TextureRole;
  width: number | null;
}
```

One embedded image of a GLB: index, role, mime type, size and pixel dimensions.

```ts
interface TextureRequest extends TextureInfo {
  bytes: number;
  data: Uint8Array;
  height: number | null;
  image: number;
  maxSize: number;
  mime: string;
  role: TextureRole;
  width: number | null;
}
```

What the texture hook gets: the image facts, its bytes and its size limit.

```ts
type TextureRole = "baseColor" | "emissive" | "normal" | "orm" | "other"
```

What a texture does in its material, which picks its size limit.

```ts
type WasmSource = URL | string | Response | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | WebAssembly.Module
```

Where the wasm core comes from: a URL to fetch, a Response, bytes or a compiled module.

```ts
function writeLock(entries: AssetEntry[]): string
```

assets.lock.json text, sorted by path.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { bakeClips, decodePack, load, optimizeModel, sampleClip, syntheticClips, syntheticGlb } from "@hackbuild/bake";

await load();
// stand ins made in code: a bumpy grid GLB and three clips on a leg rig
const { glb, report } = await optimizeModel(syntheticGlb(1, 48), { ratio: 0.5 });
console.log(report.trianglesIn, "to", report.trianglesOut, "triangles,", report.bytesIn, "to", glb.byteLength, "bytes");

const baked = bakeClips(syntheticClips(1));
for (const r of baked.report) console.log(r.name, r.maxAngleErrorDeg.toFixed(3), "degrees worst error, seam ok:", r.seamOk);

// a reader needs no wasm: decode the pack and sample a clip at 0.25 s
const pack = decodePack(baked.bytes);
const first = Object.values(pack.clips)[0]!;
const pose = new Float32Array(pack.roles.length * 4);
const root = sampleClip(pack, first, 0.25, pose);
console.log(first.name, root, pose.slice(0, 4));
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const { glb } = await optimizeModel(bytes, {
  textures: { baseColor: 1024, normal: 512 },
  resize: async (t) => (t.width && t.width > t.maxSize ? { bytes: await shrink(t.data, t.maxSize), mime: "image/webp" } : null),
});
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Calling a bake function before `await load()`; only `decodePack` and `sampleClip` work without the wasm.
- Expecting the package to resize textures: it never decodes images, so pass a `resize` hook or the images pass through.
- Feeding a Draco or meshopt compressed file, or a .gltf with external buffers: decode or embed first.
- Leaving the licence empty in a lock entry: the check fails on it, by design.
- Looking for the `hackbuild-bake` binary in node_modules: build it with cargo from the repository.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/bake: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (a bake call before `load()` resolved): `await load()` once first
- `glb: no glTF magic. only binary .glb files are read` (the file is a .gltf or not glTF): convert to a binary .glb
- `glb: only glTF 2.0 is read` (an older glTF version): export as glTF 2.0
- `glb: more than one buffer. merge buffers before baking` (several binary buffers): merge buffers in your exporter
- `glb: the buffer points at an external uri. embed it first` (an external buffer file): embed the buffer in the GLB
- `glb: <extension> geometry is compressed. decode it before baking` (Draco or meshopt compressed geometry): decode the geometry first
- `glb: ...` (missing or overrunning views and accessors) (a damaged or unusual file): check the file in a glTF validator
- `clip bake: ...` (the skeleton or a clip disagrees on role counts, fps is not above 0, or more than 8 contact roles): fix the input the message names
- `bake: clip input does not parse: ...` (the clip input could not be read): check every clip has `name` and `q`
- `bake: no HBCP magic. this is not a clip pack` (`decodePack` got another file): pass a pack from `bakeClips`
- `bake: unknown pack version` (a pack from a newer format): update the package
- `bake: the pack ends early` (a truncated pack): fetch or write the pack again

---

# @hackbuild/environment

> Light a three.js scene around a character with a key light, a rim light, image light and a set built from kit models.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/environment/

## Purpose

- Describes a scene as data: key and rim light, image light from an HDRI or the three.js room environment, a backdrop, an optional ground disk and fog, and a set of kit models.
- Ships four presets, `studio`, `room`, `cafe` and `outdoors`; the studio needs no file.
- Lists the files a preset needs, so a page can keep a scene off until its files are there.
- Loads a scene fully before it touches yours, then swaps it in with one call and restores tone mapping and exposure on dispose.
- Merges every kit mesh of the same look into one, so a room draws in a few dozen calls.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/environment three
```

The main entry has no three.js: presets, the file lists, the missing file error and the light math. `@hackbuild/environment/three` builds the lights, assembles the set and loads a scene.

| subpath | needs | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/environment` | nothing | none |
| `@hackbuild/environment/three` | `three` (optional peer) | 0.186.1 or later |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/environment

```ts
function azimuthOfU(u: number): number
```

Azimuth, radians as atan2(x, z), of the direction three.js maps to equirect column `u` (0 to 1).

```ts
function brightestAzimuth(data: ArrayLike<number>, width: number, height: number, channels?: number): number
```

Azimuth (radians, atan2(x, z)) of the brightest spot above the horizon of an equirect image in linear RGB(A) floats.


A cafe corner from the Kenney Furniture kit under a cafe HDRI.

```ts
function direction(azimuthDeg: number, elevationDeg: number): [number, number, number]
```

```ts
  backdrop: { blur: number; intensity: number } | { color: string };

  keyElevation: number;
  probe: { intensity: number; saturation: number };
  rim: { color: string; intensity: number };
  scale: number;
```

```ts
  label: string;
  layout: EnvironmentLayout;

```

A named scene: its layout, the HDRI it lights from and the licence of its kit models.

```ts
  file: string;
  licence: string;

}
```

An HDRI a preset needs, with its licence and source for the credit line.

```ts
interface LayoutItem {
  at: [number, number, number];

  model: string;
  rot?: number;
  scale?: number;
}
```

One kit model placed in a layout, in kit units, optionally repeated on a grid.

```ts
class MissingFileError extends Error {
  constructor(file: string);

}
```

An Error for a file the resolver could not give; `file` carries the path.

```ts
function missingFor(preset: Pick<EnvironmentPreset, "layout" | "hdri">, have: (file: string) => boolean): string[]
```

The files of `needsOf` that `have` does not know; empty means the preset can load.

```ts
function needsOf(preset: Pick<EnvironmentPreset, "layout" | "hdri">): string[]
```

Every file a preset needs from the caller: the HDRI, then each kit model once.

```ts
function normalizeProbe(coefficients: [number, number, number][], saturation: number): number
```

Scales nine spherical harmonic RGB coefficients in place to an average radiance of 1 and pulls each toward its luminance by `saturation` (1 keeps the color).

```ts
const outdoors: EnvironmentLayout
```

An open scene of Kenney Nature kit models on a ground disk under a sky HDRI.

```ts
function presetOf(id: string): EnvironmentPreset | undefined
```

A preset by id, or undefined.

```ts
const PRESETS: readonly EnvironmentPreset[]
```

One preset per layout, with the files each needs and their licences.

```ts
function probeMean(c0: [number, number, number]): number
```

Average radiance of a probe from its first coefficient.

```ts
const room: EnvironmentLayout
```

A furnished room from the Kenney Furniture kit under an indoor HDRI.

```ts
const studio: EnvironmentLayout
```

The studio: room environment light, a grey floor and a flat backdrop; needs no file.

### @hackbuild/environment/three

```ts
function assemble(items: readonly LayoutItem[], scale: number, load: (file: string) => Promise<Object3D<Object3DEventMap>>): Promise<Group<Object3DEventMap>>
```

Builds a set from kit models and flattens it: every mesh is baked into world space and merged with the others of the same look, so a room of fifty props draws in a couple of dozen calls.

```ts
function buildGround(ground: { color: string; radius: number }): Mesh
```

```ts
type FileSource = string | URL | ArrayBuffer | Blob
```

A loaded scene, held off screen until `attach()`.

```ts
function loadEnvironment(preset: string | EnvironmentPreset, scene: Scene, renderer: WebGLRenderer, opts?: EnvironmentOptions): Promise<LoadedEnvironment>
```

Loads a preset (or a preset id) fully without touching the scene.

```ts
function loadHdri(resolve: Resolve, file: string): Promise<DataTexture>
```

An HDRI as a float equirect texture.

```ts
function modelLoader(resolve: Resolve): (file: string) => Promise<Object3D<Object3DEventMap>>
```

```ts
function probeFrom(renderer: WebGLRenderer, source: Scene, intensity: number, saturation: number): Promise<{ mean: number; probe: LightProbe }>
```

Renders `source` into a 32 px cube and reads spherical harmonics from it, normalized to an average radiance of 1 and pulled toward grey by `saturation`; `mean` is the original average.

```ts
type Resolve = (file: string) => Promise<FileSource | null> | FileSource | null
```

Finds a file a layout needs; rejects or returns null when it is not there.

```ts
const SHADOW_EXTENT: 1.6
```

Half width of the key light's shadow camera, meters (vendor).

```ts
const SHADOW_MAP: 1024
```

Key light shadow map side, pixels (vendor).

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import * as THREE from "three";
import { missingFor, presetOf } from "@hackbuild/environment";
import { loadEnvironment } from "@hackbuild/environment/three";

const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true });
renderer.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight);
document.body.append(renderer.domElement);
const scene = new THREE.Scene();
const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(35, innerWidth / innerHeight, 0.1, 100);
camera.position.set(0, 1.2, 3.5);

// a stand in for your character: a capsule at the origin, facing +Z
scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CapsuleGeometry(0.25, 1.1), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial()).translateY(0.8));

// the studio needs no file; room, cafe and outdoors list the files they need
console.log("room needs", missingFor(presetOf("room")!, () => false));
const env = await loadEnvironment("studio", scene, renderer);
env.attach();
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => renderer.render(scene, camera));
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const files = new Map<string, Blob>(); // filled from a drop or a file input
const room = presetOf("room")!;
if (missingFor(room, (p) => files.has(p)).length === 0) {
  const env = await loadEnvironment(room, scene, renderer, { resolve: (p) => files.get(p) ?? null });
  env.attach();
}
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Do not add the loaded scene by hand or expect `loadEnvironment` to show it; call `attach()` when you want it on screen and `dispose()` on the old one.
- Do not bundle the HDRIs or kit models with your page build; give them through `resolve` from a drop or a URL and show the licence from the preset.
- Do not move the character away from the origin to fit a set; layouts are built around the origin facing +Z.
- Import `loadEnvironment` from `@hackbuild/environment/three`, not the main entry, which has no three.js.

## Errors this package throws

- `environment: could not load <file>. drop the file or pick the studio.` (`MissingFileError`: the resolver gave null, threw, or its URL did not fetch; `error.file` holds the path): give the file through `resolve`, or use the studio
- `environment: no scene named <id>.` (`loadEnvironment` got an id that is not in `PRESETS`): use `studio`, `room`, `cafe` or `outdoors`, or pass a preset object

---

# @hackbuild/gait

> Procedural locomotion for legged rigs: Froude gait choice, leg oscillators, footfall tables, posture springs, tail and ears, with a Rust core in wasm.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/gait/

## Purpose

- Picks walk, pace, trot, canter or gallop from the Froude number, with a dead band and a per animal pace bias, from validated footfall tables.
- Steps four legs with `QuadrupedGait`: a phase oscillator per leg, landing prediction, minimum jerk swings, stepping in place, and a stop that lets swinging feet land first.
- Moves the body with `BodyDynamics`: sit, down, bow and reach postures, terrain pitch and roll, gait bob, lean into turns, load shift and breathing.
- Adds a tail (`TailWag`, eight wag modes), ears (`Ears`) and obstacle steering (`steer`).
- Drives a three.js quadruped under `/three`: `measureQuadruped` reads the rig, `driveQuadruped` writes each frame with two bone leg IK.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/gait
```

three.js is an optional peer, needed only for the `/three` subpath.

| subpath | what | needs |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/gait` | gait, body, tail, ears, steering, the backend interface | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/gait/three` | `measureQuadruped`, `driveQuadruped` | `three` 0.186.1 or later (optional peer) |
| `@hackbuild/gait/wasm` | the wasm file, for `load(url)` | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/gait/inline` | the wasm as base64, what `load()` uses with no argument | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/gait/iife` | `dist/gait.iife.js`, a classic script setting `HackbuildGait` | `THREE` on the page for the adapter |

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { load, QuadrupedGait, type LegSpec } from "@hackbuild/gait";

await load(); // the wasm core is inlined; load() also takes a URL or bytes

// four legs (LF RF LH RH) in the body frame, meters: x to the left, z forward
const legs: LegSpec[] = [
  { x: 0.09, z: 0.22, toe: 0.02, front: true },
  { x: -0.09, z: 0.22, toe: 0.02, front: true },
  { x: 0.09, z: -0.2, toe: 0.02, front: false },
  { x: -0.09, z: -0.2, toe: 0.02, front: false },
];
let seed = 1;
const rng = () => (seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647; // any seeded () => number
const gait = new QuadrupedGait(legs, 0.42, { rng });

// walk forward at 1.2 m/s for 2 seconds at 60 frames per second
const pose = { x: 0, z: 0, yaw: 0 };
for (let frame = 0; frame < 120; frame++) {
  pose.z += 1.2 / 60;
  const s = gait.update(1 / 60, pose, { speed: 1.2, turnRate: 0 });
  const main = Object.entries(s.weights).sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1])[0]?.[0];
  if (frame % 30 === 29) console.log(`${main}, froude ${s.froude.toFixed(2)}, feet down ${s.feet.filter((f) => f.stance).length}`);
}
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { BodyDynamics, QuadrupedGait, TailWag } from "@hackbuild/gait";
import { driveQuadruped, measureQuadruped } from "@hackbuild/gait/three";

const rig = measureQuadruped(dog, names); // dog at the origin, facing +Z, in its rest pose
const gait = new QuadrupedGait(rig.specs, rig.legLength, { ground: heightAt, rng });
const body = new BodyDynamics(rig.geometry, rng);
const tail = new TailWag(3, 0.06, rng);
function frame(dt: number, pose: { x: number; z: number; yaw: number }, cmd = { speed: 1.2, turnRate: 0 }) {
  const s = gait.update(dt, pose, cmd);
  const b = body.update(dt, s, cmd, gait.nominal(pose.x, pose.z, pose.yaw).map(([x, z]) => heightAt(x, z)));
  gait.setOffsets(b.legOffsets);
  driveQuadruped(rig, pose, s, b, { tail: tail.update(dt, { modeWeights: [1, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1], arousal: 0.4 }) });
}
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Making a class before `await load()`.
- Calling `measureQuadruped` on a posed or turned model; the root must sit at the origin with identity rotation, facing +Z, in its rest pose.
- Moving the body without telling the gait: pass the same pose you move the root by to `update` each frame.
- Skipping `gait.setOffsets(body.legOffsets)`; postures then leave the feet where they stood.
- Dropping a `QuadrupedGait`, `BodyDynamics`, `TailWag` or `Ears` without `dispose()`; each holds wasm memory.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/gait: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (a class was made before `load()` resolved): `await load()` once at start up
- `gait: no bone named <name>` (`measureQuadruped` found no object with a name you passed): check the names against the model; `limbChains` from `@hackbuild/rig` lists them
- a `WebAssembly` compile or fetch error (`load(url)` pointed at a missing or wrong file): call `load()` with no argument, or check the URL serves `gait_bg.wasm`

---

# @hackbuild/ik

> Inverse kinematics for characters on the web: two bone, FABRIK, CCD, clamped look at, finger curl and foot locking, with a Rust core in wasm.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/ik/

## Purpose

- Solves arms and legs analytically with `twoBone`, bending toward a pole direction, with an optional soft reach.
- Solves longer chains with `fabrik` (cone and hinge limits) or `ccd` (a step cap per joint), and turns a solved chain back into bone rotations with `segmentDeltas`.
- Aims a head over a spine, neck and head chain with yaw and pitch limits (`lookAngles`, `lookChain`), and hands what the neck cannot take to the body.
- Builds a palm frame and grip point and curls fingers and thumb (`handCurl`).
- Holds a foot where it landed while it bears weight and releases it smoothly (`ContactLock`), with the hip drop that keeps a locked foot in reach (`pelvisDrop`).

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/ik
```

three.js is an optional peer, needed only for the `/three` subpath.

| subpath | what | needs |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/ik` | solvers on plain arrays | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/ik/three` | `solveTwoBone`, `solveChain`, `lookAtChain`, `curlFingers`, `FootLock`, `rotateWorld` on three.js objects | `three` 0.186.1 or later (optional peer) |
| `@hackbuild/ik/wasm` | the wasm file, for `load(url)` | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/ik/inline` | the wasm as base64, what `load()` uses with no argument | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/ik/iife` | `dist/ik.iife.js`, a classic script setting `HackbuildIk` | `THREE` on the page for the adapter |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/ik

```ts
function ccd(positions: Vec3[], target: Vec3, opts?: ChainOptions & { maxStep?: number }): SolveInfo
```

CCD in place on `positions`; `maxStep` caps radians per joint per pass.

```ts
interface ChainOptions {
  iterations?: number;
  tolerance?: number;
}
```

Iteration cap and goal tolerance in meters for `fabrik` and `ccd`.

```ts
function clampDirection(head: Quat, dir: Vec3, maxYaw?: number, maxPitch?: number): Vec3
```

A direction limited to within the given yaw and pitch of the head's forward.

```ts
class ContactLock {

  locked(): boolean;
  update(dt: number, target: Float64Array, contact: number, out: Float64Array): void;
}
```

Holds a foot where it landed while contact is high and releases it smoothly when contact drops.

```ts
const DEFAULT_LOOK_LIMITS: LookLimits
```

Head limits: yaw within 1.25 rad either side, pitch from 0.8 rad down to 0.6 rad up.

A palm frame, the grip point, and the curl axes and angles for the fingers and thumb.

```ts
type JointLimit = { kind: "none" } | { kind: "cone"; max: number } | { axis: Vec3; kind: "hinge" }
```

A joint limit for `fabrik`: none, a cone of `max` radians around the parent segment, or a hinge around `axis`.

```ts
function loadSync(source: ArrayBuffer | Module | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>): void
```

Loads the wasm synchronously from bytes or a compiled module.

```ts
function lookChain(frame: Quat, yaw: number, pitch: number, weights: readonly number[]): Quat[]
```

World deltas that share yaw and pitch over a chain by weight; apply parent first.

```ts
interface LookLimits {
  pitchMax: number;

  yawMax: number;
  yawMin: number;
}
```

Yaw and pitch limits in radians for a look at, measured from the frame's forward.

```ts
interface LookResult {
```

```ts
function pelvisDrop(hip: Vec3, foot: Vec3, reach: number, up?: Vec3): number
```

```ts
type Quat = [number, number, number, number]
```

A rotation as a unit quaternion `[x, y, z, w]`.

```ts
interface SolveInfo {

}
```

```ts
function twoBone(a: Vec3, b: Vec3, c: Vec3, target: Vec3, pole: Vec3, soft?: number): TwoBoneResult
```

Two bone solve of root `a`, middle `b`, end `c` toward `target`, bending toward the `pole` direction.

```ts
interface TwoBoneResult {

  mid: Vec3;
  reached: boolean;
  upper: Quat;
}
```

```ts
type Vec3 = [number, number, number]
```

A point or direction as `[x, y, z]` in meters, +Y up.

```ts
type WasmSource = URL | string | Response | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | WebAssembly.Module
```

Where the wasm comes from: a URL or path to fetch, a Response, the bytes, or a compiled module.

### @hackbuild/ik/three

Curls the fingers of one hand by `amount` (0 open, 1 a fist).

```ts
interface FingerBones {
```

```ts

```

Premultiplies a world rotation delta onto an object, keeping its parent.

```ts
function solveChain(bones: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>[], target: Vector3, opts?: { iterations?: number; limits?: JointLimit[]; method?: "fabrik" | "ccd"; tolerance?: number }): number
```

FABRIK or CCD on a bone chain (root first, last bone is the end effector).

```ts
function solveTwoBone(upper: Object3D, lower: Object3D, end: Object3D, target: Vector3, pole: Vector3, opts?: { soft?: number; weight?: number }): boolean
```

Two bone IK on three bones toward a world `target`, bending toward the world `pole` direction.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { DEFAULT_LOOK_LIMITS, load, lookAngles, twoBone, type Vec3 } from "@hackbuild/ik";

// the wasm core is inlined; load() also takes a URL or bytes
await load();

// a left leg in meters, +Y up, +Z forward: hip, knee, ankle
const hip: Vec3 = [0.1, 0.9, 0];
const knee: Vec3 = [0.1, 0.5, 0];
const ankle: Vec3 = [0.1, 0.1, 0];
// put the foot on a step 20 cm up and 15 cm ahead, knee bending forward
const leg = twoBone(hip, knee, ankle, [0.1, 0.3, 0.15], [0, 0, 1]);
console.log("knee", leg.mid, "foot reached", leg.reached);

// head at 1.6 m facing +Z (identity frame) looking at a point up and to the left
const look = lookAngles([0, 0, 0, 1], [0, 1.6, 0], [1, 1.9, 1], DEFAULT_LOOK_LIMITS);
console.log(`yaw ${look.yaw.toFixed(2)} rad, pitch ${look.pitch.toFixed(2)} rad, clamped ${look.clamped}`);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { FootLock, lookAtChain, solveTwoBone } from "@hackbuild/ik/three";

const lock = new FootLock(); // holds while contact is above 0.55
function frame(dt: number) {
  lock.update(dt, footTarget, contact);
  solveTwoBone(bones.leftUpperLeg, bones.leftLowerLeg, bones.leftFoot, footTarget, kneeForward);
  lookAtChain([bones.neck, bones.head], [0.4, 0.6], camera.position, body.quaternion);
}
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Calling a solver before `await load()`.
- Mixing units: positions are meters in one space, +Y up and +Z forward; a rig in centimeters needs scaling first (see `@hackbuild/rig` `analyzeRest`).
- Applying the deltas child first; apply each world delta parent first, as `segmentDeltas` and `lookChain` order them.
- Passing `prevYaw` as 0 every frame; pass last frame's `yaw + bodyYaw`, or a target crossing behind the head flips sides.
- Forgetting `free()` on a `ContactLock` you no longer use (or `dispose()` on `FootLock`); it holds wasm memory.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/ik: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (a solver ran before `load()` resolved): `await load()` once at start up
- a `WebAssembly` compile or fetch error (`load(url)` pointed at a missing or wrong file): call `load()` with no argument to use the inlined copy, or check the URL serves `ik_bg.wasm`

---

# @hackbuild/lipsync

> Move a character's mouth from speech timings or the audio level, out to Oculus visemes, VRM vowels or ARKit blendshapes.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/lipsync/

## Purpose

- Turns word, phoneme and viseme events from a TTS engine into a viseme timeline, with ARPAbet, IPA or Oculus phoneme names.
- Blends neighbouring visemes by dominance, so p, b and m still close the lips between two open vowels.
- Spells words with no phonemes into visemes by English letter rules, in real time as words arrive.
- Falls back to the audio level when no timings cover the moment, with a rough vowel shape from three formant bands.
- Reads the bellows voice's phoneme spans or its vocal tract state through two subpaths, with no import of bellows.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/lipsync
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/rig` for the one expression and viseme table. It needs no three.js and no Web Audio: you pass levels or analyser arrays.

| subpath | drives it | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/lipsync` | speech events, audio level | none |
| `@hackbuild/lipsync/bellows` | `bellows-voice` plans (optional peer, structural types only) | 0.8.0, `bellowsjs` 0.5.0 |
| `@hackbuild/lipsync/articulatory` | `bellows-voice` articulator frames, probe or `TractModel` (optional peer, structural types only) | 0.8.0 |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/lipsync/articulatory

```ts
function arkitFromChannels(c: MouthChannels, out?: Map<"eyeBlinkLeft" | "eyeLookDownLeft" | "eyeLookInLeft" | "eyeLookOutLeft" | "eyeLookUpLeft" | "eyeSquintLeft" | "eyeWideLeft" | "eyeBlinkRight" | "eyeLookDownRight" | "eyeLookInRight" | "eyeLookOutRight" | "eyeLookUpRight" | "eyeSquintRight" | "eyeWideRight" | "jawForward" | "jawLeft" | "jawRight" | "jawOpen" | "mouthClose" | "mouthFunnel" | "mouthPucker" | "mouthLeft" | "mouthRight" | "mouthSmileLeft" | "mouthSmileRight" | "mouthFrownLeft" | "mouthFrownRight" | "mouthDimpleLeft" | "mouthDimpleRight" | "mouthStretchLeft" | "mouthStretchRight" | "mouthRollLower" | "mouthRollUpper" | "mouthShrugLower" | "mouthShrugUpper" | "mouthPressLeft" | "mouthPressRight" | "mouthLowerDownLeft" | "mouthLowerDownRight" | "mouthUpperUpLeft" | "mouthUpperUpRight" | "browDownLeft" | "browDownRight" | "browInnerUp" | "browOuterUpLeft" | "browOuterUpRight" | "cheekPuff" | "cheekSquintLeft" | "cheekSquintRight" | "noseSneerLeft" | "noseSneerRight" | "tongueOut", number>): Map<"eyeBlinkLeft" | "eyeLookDownLeft" | "eyeLookInLeft" | "eyeLookOutLeft" | "eyeLookUpLeft" | "eyeSquintLeft" | "eyeWideLeft" | "eyeBlinkRight" | "eyeLookDownRight" | "eyeLookInRight" | "eyeLookOutRight" | "eyeLookUpRight" | "eyeSquintRight" | "eyeWideRight" | "jawForward" | "jawLeft" | "jawRight" | "jawOpen" | "mouthClose" | "mouthFunnel" | "mouthPucker" | "mouthLeft" | "mouthRight" | "mouthSmileLeft" | "mouthSmileRight" | "mouthFrownLeft" | "mouthFrownRight" | "mouthDimpleLeft" | "mouthDimpleRight" | "mouthStretchLeft" | "mouthStretchRight" | "mouthRollLower" | "mouthRollUpper" | "mouthShrugLower" | "mouthShrugUpper" | "mouthPressLeft" | "mouthPressRight" | "mouthLowerDownLeft" | "mouthLowerDownRight" | "mouthUpperUpLeft" | "mouthUpperUpRight" | "browDownLeft" | "browDownRight" | "browInnerUp" | "browOuterUpLeft" | "browOuterUpRight" | "cheekPuff" | "cheekSquintLeft" | "cheekSquintRight" | "noseSneerLeft" | "noseSneerRight" | "tongueOut", number>
```

ARKit blendshape weights straight from the channels: jawOpen from the jaw, mouthClose from the lip closure, pucker when rounded with a small aperture and funnel when rounded and open, stretch and a little smile when spread, mouthRollLower for f and v, tongueOut for th.


The five VRM vowel presets as points in (open, round, spread), taken from bellows-voice's own targets: aa the open back vowel, ee the mean of e and the open-mid front vowel, ih the close front vowel, oh o, ou u.

```ts

```

Weights of the five vowels for a channel set: a softmax of negative squared distance, summing to 1.

### @hackbuild/lipsync

Writes a frame to a face: VRM vowel presets, `viseme_*` morphs (Ready Player Me style), or ARKit blendshapes built from the vowel composites plus `mouthClose` for lip closures.


```ts
  end: number;
  start: number;
  viseme: "sil" | "PP" | "FF" | "TH" | "DD" | "kk" | "CH" | "SS" | "nn" | "RR" | "aa" | "E" | "I" | "O" | "U";
}
```

```ts
class VisemeTimeline {
  constructor();

  clear(): void;
  prune(t: number, keep?: number): void;
  push(events: SpeechEvent | readonly SpeechEvent[]): void;

}
```

Timed visemes built from speech events and sampled with coarticulation.

```ts
function vowelFromBands(b: Bands): Record<VrmVowel, number>
```

A rough vowel shape from band energies (inferred from formant ranges): strong high band means a front vowel (ee, ih), a low band with little mid means a rounded vowel (oh, ou), otherwise an open aa.

```ts
const VRM_VOWELS: readonly ["aa", "ih", "ou", "ee", "oh"]
```

The five VRM mouth vowel presets.

```ts
type VrmVowel = typeof VRM_VOWELS[number]
```

One VRM mouth vowel preset.

```ts

```

Letters to visemes with relative lengths, for engines that give word timings only.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { LipSync, OCULUS_VISEMES, drive, type ExpressionSink } from "@hackbuild/lipsync";

const lips = new LipSync();
// word timings as a TTS engine reports them, in seconds on your clock
lips.push([
  { type: "word", time: 0.0, end: 0.35, text: "hello" },
  { type: "word", time: 0.4, end: 0.8, text: "mama" },
]);

// any object with setValue: an avatar ExpressionRig or a three-vrm expression manager
const face = new Map<string, number>();
const sink: ExpressionSink = { setValue: (name, weight) => face.set(name, weight) };

for (let t = 0; t <= 1; t += 1 / 30) {
  const frame = lips.update(t, 1 / 30);
  const top = frame.visemes.indexOf(Math.max(...frame.visemes));
  console.log(t.toFixed(2), frame.source, OCULUS_VISEMES[top], frame.open.toFixed(2));
  drive(sink, frame, "vrm"); // face now holds aa, ih, ou, ee, oh
}
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const buf = new Uint8Array(analyser.fftSize);
analyser.getByteTimeDomainData(buf);
lips.setLevel(rms(buf));
drive(avatar.expressions, lips.update(ctx.currentTime, dt), "vrm");
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const plan = alto.speak("Shall we meet at noon?");
lips.push(fromSungPlan(plan)); // live plans are on the context clock, offset 0
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Do not mix clocks: event `time` and the `t` you pass to `update` must be on the same clock, usually the AudioContext's.
- Do not pass an offset to `fromSungPlan` for a live bellows plan; live plans are already on the context clock. Pass the play time only for an offline render that starts at 0.
- Do not import bellows-voice just to type the calls; the subpaths read its plans and frames by shape, so pass what the engine returns.
- Call `stop()` when speech is cut short, or the rest of the timeline keeps moving the mouth.

## Errors this package throws

- none; `frame.source` stays `"silent"` (no event covers `t` and the level is under the gate): check `t` and the event times are on the same clock; raise the level or lower `gate`
- none; the mouth trails the sound (events pushed on a different clock, or `lead` too small): pass `ctx.currentTime` based times; raise `lead` from 0.04 s
- none; the mouth flutters on breath (the level gate is too low): raise `gate` from 0.015

---

# @hackbuild/motion-match

> Motion matching over a clip database, with inertialized transitions, on a Rust core compiled to wasm.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/motion-match/

## Purpose

- Builds a feature database from your clips: future trajectory positions and facing, foot positions and velocities, and hip velocity, each in the frame's root space.
- Searches it by brute force or with a two level bounding box search that returns the same frame and cost, every 0.1 s by default.
- Plays the matched clip, moves the root by the clip's own root step, and blends every jump with inertialization on bone rotations, hips and feet.
- Turns a speed and turn rate into a desired trajectory, or takes a trajectory you build.
- Stands in for the procedural gait: `MotionMatcher` implements the same locomotion backend contract as `@hackbuild/gait`.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/motion-match
```

No dependencies and no peers. The wasm core loads from the package's own file, a URL or bytes you pass, or an inlined copy.

| subpath | what |
|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/motion-match` | the matcher, clip set and backend contract |
| `@hackbuild/motion-match/wasm` | the wasm file, to pass to `load()` as a URL |
| `@hackbuild/motion-match/inline` | the wasm as base64, for builds with no fetch |
| `@hackbuild/motion-match/iife` | the single file build, global `HackbuildMotionMatch`, wasm inlined |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/motion-match

```ts
interface Capabilities {
  headPitchBias: number;

  turnInPlace: boolean;
}
```

```ts
type WasmSource = URL | string | Response | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | WebAssembly.Module
```
