## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { ClipSet, load, MotionMatcher } from "@hackbuild/motion-match";

await load();
// a clip database made in code: three steady gaits, a start and a stop
const clips = new ClipSet(30);
for (const speed of [0.6, 1.2, 2]) clips.addSynthetic({ speed });
clips.addSynthetic({ speed: 0, speedEnd: 1.2 });
clips.addSynthetic({ speed: 1.2, speedEnd: 0 });
const matcher = new MotionMatcher(clips);

// one second at 60 frames a second, asking for a gentle left turn
for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) {
  const root = matcher.update(1 / 60, { speed: 1.2, turnRate: 0.4 });
  const pose = matcher.pose(); // local rotations, hips and feet in the root frame
  if (i % 20 === 0) console.log(root.x.toFixed(2), root.z.toFixed(2), matcher.last.clip, pose.feet.length);
}
console.log(matcher.last.transitions, "transitions,", matcher.motorState().contacts);
matcher.dispose();
clips.dispose();
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const matcher = new MotionMatcher(clips, { capabilities: { turnInPlace: true }, params: { searchInterval: 0.05 } });
const frame = matcher.step(1 / 60, matcher.trajectory(1.5, 0));
if (frame.jumped) console.log("now clip", frame.clip, "frame", frame.frame);
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Calling `new ClipSet()` before `await load()`: every class needs the wasm core.
- Mixing rigs in one `ClipSet`: all clips must share bones and feet; retarget them first.
- Expecting locked feet: the matcher does not pin planted feet, so add `FootLock` from `@hackbuild/ik` on top.
- Forgetting `dispose()` on the matcher and the set: they hold wasm memory.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/motion-match: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (a `ClipSet`, `MotionMatcher` or `goldenTrace` call before `load()` resolved): `await load()` once before building anything
- an error from `ClipSet.add` (the arrays of a clip disagree on frame, bone or foot counts): give every array the same frame count and every clip the same bones and feet

---

# @hackbuild/motion-net

> Run the published quadruped categorical codebook matching network in the browser and drive a dog's gait from it.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/motion-net/

## Purpose

- Loads the network's JSON manifest and flat binary from a URL, bytes or a File, checks the SHA-256 when you give one, and checks every tensor's dtype, shape, count, alignment and range before anything runs.
- Runs the forward pass (code estimate, three refinement passes, a time conditioned decoder for 16 frames) in Rust on wasm SIMD128, in a blob worker or in the page when a worker is refused.
- Drives a dog with `QuadrupedHost`: turns a speed and turn command into network inputs, plays predictions back in time, integrates root motion and pins planted paws.
- Implements the locomotion backend contract of `@hackbuild/gait`, so the network can stand in for the procedural gait.
- States the weight licence once per page before the first load; no weights ship in the package or on the demo site.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/motion-net
```

No dependencies and no peers. The host gives bone positions and rotations as plain arrays, so any renderer can draw the dog.

| subpath | what |
|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/motion-net` | weights, predictor, host, layout constants |
| `@hackbuild/motion-net/wasm` | the wasm file, to pass as `wasm` to `Predictor.create` or to `load()` |
| `@hackbuild/motion-net/inline` | the wasm as base64, used when you pass nothing |
| `@hackbuild/motion-net/iife` | the single file build, global `HackbuildMotionNet`, wasm inlined |

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { loadWeights, Predictor, QuadrupedHost } from "@hackbuild/motion-net";

// the weights are not in this package: give their urls as ?manifest=<url>&bin=<url>
const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const manifest = q.get("manifest");
const bin = q.get("bin");
if (!manifest || !bin) throw new Error("give the weight urls as ?manifest=<url>&bin=<url>");
// onLicence gets the weights' own licence line (non commercial) before anything runs
const weights = await loadWeights({ manifest, bin, onLicence: (line) => document.body.append(line) });
const predictor = await Predictor.create(weights); // a blob worker, or the page when workers are refused
const host = new QuadrupedHost(predictor, weights.styles);

let last = performance.now();
function frame(now: number) {
  const root = host.update((now - last) / 1000, { speed: 1.2, turnRate: 0.3 });
  last = now;
  document.title = `${root.speed.toFixed(2)} m/s, ${host.motorState().contacts.filter(Boolean).length} paws down`;
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
requestAnimationFrame(frame);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { loadWeights, UPSTREAM } from "@hackbuild/motion-net";

const weights = await loadWeights({ manifest: UPSTREAM.manifest, bin: UPSTREAM.bin, sha256: UPSTREAM.binSha256, onProgress: (n, total) => console.log(n, total) });
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Bundling, committing or hosting the weights: they are CC BY-NC 4.0 and load at run time from a URL or a File the user gives.
- Using the weights in a commercial product: the licence forbids it, whatever this package's MIT code allows.
- Calling `load()` and expecting the predictor to use that copy: `Predictor.create` loads its own wasm, from `wasm` or the inlined copy.
- Reading bone axes as the normalized humanoid's: the 27 bone dog keeps its source rig's conventions; retarget it yourself.
- Calling `update` with no frame time: pass seconds since the last frame; the host plays predictions on that clock.

## Errors this package throws

- `motion-net: could not fetch <url>: ...` (the network refused the weight URL (offline, CORS)): check the URL and that its host allows your origin
- `motion-net: fetch <url> answered <status>` (the weight or wasm URL answered an error): check the URL
- `motion-net: the manifest is not JSON` (the manifest part is not the JSON manifest): pass `quadruped.json`, or a parsed manifest object
- `motion-net: sha-256 of the binary is <hash>, expected <hash>` (the binary differs from the one you named): download it again, or check the `sha256` you passed
- `motion-net: the weights do not match the format: ...` (a tensor is missing or has the wrong dtype, shape, count, offset or range): use the manifest and binary that belong together; `validate` lists every mismatch
- `motion-net: model.<key> is missing or not a positive integer` (the manifest's model section is incomplete): check the manifest
- `motion-net: no network worker. <reason>.` (`worker: true` and no worker could start): use `worker: "auto"` to fall back to the page
- `motion-net: the input has <n> values, the network takes <m> values` (`predict` got an input of the wrong length): pass 339 values, the layout in `IN`
- `motion-net: the predictor was disposed. the run was dropped.` (a run asked for after `dispose()`): create a new predictor
- `@hackbuild/motion-net: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (`goldenTrace` before `load()`): `await load()`; the predictor loads its own copy

---

# @hackbuild/motion-views

> Put a character stage, an avatar drop card and a clip strip on your page, drawn with the hackbuild-ui stylesheet, as custom elements or Vue components.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/motion-views/

## Purpose

- `CharacterStage`: a body on a lit stage with idle, gaze, blinks and lips, a corner plate, turn around and framing tools, a verb row and an inset slot. It speaks real audio with word timings, or text alone on estimated timings.
- `AvatarDrop`: a drop zone and pick button that loads a VRM, GLB or FBX once, checks its rig in plain words, draws a still and shows the avatar card.
- `ClipStrip`: each clip's still, name and length, the picked one pressed and one play button.
- Ships every view as a mount function, a custom element and a Vue 3 component, on one code path.
- Carries no styles of its own; every class is hackbuild-ui's.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/motion-views three @virgilvox/hackbuild-ui
```

`@virgilvox/hackbuild-ui` 0.10 is a required peer, and the page loads its stylesheet (`@virgilvox/hackbuild-ui/styles.css`). three.js is needed by the views; Vue only by `/vue`. It depends on `@hackbuild/avatar`, `@hackbuild/avatar-host`, `@hackbuild/presence`, `@hackbuild/lipsync` and `@hackbuild/organic`, which install with it.

| subpath | needs | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/motion-views` | nothing; the words, clip items and speech timings | none |
| `@hackbuild/motion-views/vanilla` | `three` (optional peer), `@virgilvox/hackbuild-ui` (peer) | three 0.186.1 or later, hackbuild-ui `>=0.10.0 <0.11.0` |
| `@hackbuild/motion-views/vue` | `vue` (optional peer) and the above | vue 3.5.0 or later |
| `@hackbuild/motion-views/iife` | `THREE` on the page | one classic script |

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { avatarDrop, characterStage } from "@hackbuild/motion-views/vanilla";

// the stage shows a placeholder body built in code until you give it one
const host = document.createElement("div");
host.style.height = "480px";
document.body.append(host);
const stage = characterStage(host, { name: "stand-in", hello: "hello. drop a vrm, glb or fbx on me." });
stage.on((e) => e.type === "doing" && console.log("doing", e.word));

// a drop card: press the card of a checked avatar to put it on the stage
const card = document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div"));
avatarDrop(card).on((e) => {
  if (e.type === "checked") console.log(e.report.check.head, e.report.size);
  if (e.type === "use") void stage.show(e.files);
});

// text alone moves the lips on estimated word timings, with no sound
await stage.say("you can drop a model on me");
stage.gesture("wave");
```

### from the concepts

```ts
defineMotionViews({ stage: { vrm: () => import("@hackbuild/avatar/vrm").then((m) => m.vrmHook()) } });
const stage = document.querySelector<CharacterStageElement>("hb-character-stage")!;
document.querySelector("hb-avatar-drop")!.addEventListener("picked", (e) => stage.handle?.show((e as CustomEvent).detail.files));
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Load the hackbuild-ui stylesheet on the page; the views add no styles and look broken without it.
- Call `defineMotionViews()` once before using the elements; importing `/vanilla` defines nothing.
- Pass the VRM hook (`vrm: () => import("@hackbuild/avatar/vrm").then((m) => m.vrmHook())`) to read VRM files as VRM; without it a .vrm loads as plain glTF.
- Call `dispose()` on a handle you mount yourself; it stops the audio and frees the stage.

## Errors this package throws

- a `failed` event from CharacterStage (the body could not load from the URL or files): read `e.message`; give the model with its textures, or a VRM, GLB or FBX
- a `failed` event from AvatarDrop (the dropped files held no body it could read): drop a .vrm, .glb, .gltf with its .bin and textures, or .fbx
- `-1` from `play` (the clip cannot play on this body): check the body has the bones the clip moves
- `false` from `gesture` (the body lacks the bones the gesture needs): check the rig check lines of the body

---

# @hackbuild/organic

> Critically damped springs, inertialization, seeded noise and samplers for procedural animation, with a Rust core in wasm.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/organic/

## Purpose

- Moves a value toward a goal with springs set by half life: `spring`, `decay`, `velocitySpring`, `springDamper`, and `SpringBank` for many springs per frame in wasm.
- Blends from one pose to the next with offset inertialization: `Inertializer` on flat arrays, `PoseInertializer` on three.js bones.
- Draws seeded noise (`OU`, `Pink`, `NoiseBank`) and samples (`sample.gauss`, `exGaussian`, `vonMises`, `poissonGap`, `eventInStep` and more), all from one injected random source.
- Smooths targets through a cascade of first order lags (`CascadeBank`), exact at any step rate, for jaw and lip motion.
- Keeps a body clock with a daily drive and sleep pressure (`BodyClock`).

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/organic
```

three.js is an optional peer, needed only for the `/three` subpath.

| subpath | what | needs |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/organic` | springs, samplers, noise, inertializer, cascade, body clock | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/organic/three` | `PoseInertializer` over three.js bones | `three` 0.186.1 or later (optional peer) |
| `@hackbuild/organic/wasm` | the wasm file, for `load(url)` | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/organic/inline` | the wasm as base64, what `load()` uses with no argument | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/organic/iife` | `dist/organic.iife.js`, a classic script setting `HackbuildOrganic` | `THREE` on the page for the adapter |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/organic

```ts
class BodyClock {
  constructor(minutes: number, rate: number);
  asleep: boolean;
  minutes: number;
  pressure: number;
  rate: number;
  circadian(): number;
  day(): number;
  hour(): number;
  sleepiness(): number;
  tick(dt: number): void;
}
```

Game time, circadian drive and sleep pressure (two process model).

```ts
class CascadeBank {
  [key: number]: () => void;
  constructor(channels: number, step_rate_hz: number, order: number);
  channels(): number;
  free(): void;
  order(): number;
  place(i: number, value: number): void;
  setRate(i: number, per_second: number): void;
  setTarget(i: number, target: number): void;
  setTargets(targets: Float64Array): void;
  setTime(i: number, seconds: number): void;
  snap(i: number, value: number): void;
  step(steps: number, out: Float64Array): void;
  value(i: number): number;
  velocity(i: number): number;
}
```

Target approximation smoothing, many channels at a fixed step rate (ported from bellows-voice, MIT).

```ts
function decay(s: SpringState, halflife: number, dt: number, exact?: boolean): number
```

Decays an offset toward zero, the inertialization core.

```ts
function fastNegexp(x: number): number
```

A rational approximation of `exp(-x)` for x of 0 or more, used when `exact` is false.

```ts
function goldenTrace(seed: number): Float64Array
```

The golden scenario run in wasm, for the native and wasm agreement test.

```ts
function halflifeToDamping(halflife: number): number
```

The damping constant for a half life in seconds, the time the spring takes to cover half the distance to its goal.

```ts
function hashSeed(s: string): number
```

FNV-1a over UTF-16 code units, equal to the Rust `hash_seed`.

```ts
class Inertializer {
  [key: number]: () => void;
  constructor(rotations: number, positions: number);
  active(): boolean;
  apply(rot: Float64Array, pos: Float64Array, dt: number, halflife: number): void;
  capture(): void;
  free(): void;
  setFast(fast: boolean): void;
}
```

Offset inertialization over flat rotation and position arrays.

```ts
function keyed(t: number, keys: readonly readonly [number, number][]): number
```

Piecewise minimum jerk through [time, value] keys sorted by time.

```ts
function load(source?: WasmSource): Promise<void>
```

Loads the wasm.

```ts
function loadSync(source: ArrayBuffer | Module | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>): void
```

Loads the wasm synchronously from bytes or a compiled module.

```ts
function minimumJerk(t: number): number
```

Minimum jerk profile on t in 0 to 1.

```ts
class NoiseBank {
  [key: number]: () => void;
  constructor(seed: number);
  addOu(tau: number, sigma: number, mu: number): number;
  addPink(tau0: number, octaves: number): number;
  free(): void;
  step(dt: number, out: Float64Array): void;
  uniform(): number;
}
```

A bank of OU and pink channels sharing one seeded stream.

```ts
class OU {
  constructor(tau: number, sigma: number, mu: number, rng: Rng);
  mu: number;
  sigma: number;
  tau: number;
  x: number;
  step(dt: number): number;
}
```

Ornstein Uhlenbeck noise with the exact discrete update.

```ts
class Pink {
  constructor(tau0: number, octaves: number, rng: Rng);
  x: number;
  step(dt: number): number;
}
```

Summed OU octaves: an approximately 1/f drift with unit variance.

```ts
type Rng = () => number
```

Uniform numbers in [0, 1).

```ts
const sample: { eventInStep: (rate: number, dt: number, rng: Rng) => boolean; exGaussian: (mu: number, sigma: number, tau: number, rng: Rng) => number; gamma: (k: number, theta: number, rng: Rng) => number; gauss: (rng: Rng) => number; logNormal: (median: number, sigma: number, rng: Rng) => number; poissonGap: (rate: number, rng: Rng) => number; truncatedPowerLaw: (min: number, mu: number, max: number, rng: Rng) => number; vonMises: (kappa: number, rng: Rng) => number; weightedIndex: (weights: readonly number[], rng: Rng) => number }
```

Samplers.

```ts
function seededRng(seed: string | number): Rng
```

Mulberry32, the same stream as the Rust `Mulberry32` and the wasm `SeededRng`.

```ts
class SeededRng {
  [key: number]: () => void;
  constructor(seed: number);
  exGaussian(mu: number, sigma: number, tau: number): number;
  fill(out: Float64Array): void;
  free(): void;
  gamma(k: number, theta: number): number;
  gauss(): number;
  logNormal(median: number, sigma: number): number;
  next(): number;
  poissonGap(rate: number): number;
  truncatedPowerLaw(min: number, mu: number, max: number): number;
  vonMises(kappa: number): number;
}
```

Seeded Mulberry32 stream with the samplers on it.

```ts
function spring(s: SpringState, goal: number, halflife: number, dt: number, exact?: boolean): number
```

Critically damped spring toward `goal`.

```ts
class SpringBank {
  [key: number]: () => void;
  constructor(n: number);
  free(): void;
  isEmpty(): boolean;
  len(): number;
  positions(): Float64Array;
  setPositions(x: Float64Array): void;
  step(goals: Float64Array, halflife: number, dt: number, fast: boolean, out: Float64Array): void;
  stepEach(goals: Float64Array, halflives: Float64Array, dt: number, fast: boolean, out: Float64Array): void;
  velocities(): Float64Array;
}
```

Many scalar springs stepped in one call.

```ts
function springDamper(s: SpringState, goal: number, vGoal: number, ratio: number, halflife: number, dt: number): number
```

Spring damper with a damping ratio (1 critical, below 1 overshoots).

```ts
function springState(x?: number): SpringState
```

A spring state at rest at `x` (default 0).

```ts
interface SpringState {
  a: number;
  v: number;
  x: number;
}
```

Position `x`, velocity `v` and acceleration `a` of one scalar spring, changed in place by the spring calls.

```ts
function velocitySpring(s: SpringState, vGoal: number, halflife: number, dt: number, exact?: boolean): number
```

Velocity eases toward `vGoal`; position integrates it exactly.

```ts
type WasmSource = URL | string | Response | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | WebAssembly.Module
```

Where the wasm comes from: a URL or path to fetch, a Response, the bytes, or a compiled module.

### @hackbuild/organic/three

```ts
class PoseInertializer {
  constructor(bones: (Object3D<Object3DEventMap> | Bone<Object3DEventMap> | null | undefined)[], opts?: PoseInertializerOptions);
  readonly active: boolean;
  apply(dt: number, halflife: number): void;
  capture(): void;
  dispose(): void;
}
```

Call `capture()` at a transition, then `apply(dt, halflife)` every frame after the new pose has been written to the bones.

```ts
interface PoseInertializerOptions {
  fast?: boolean;
  positions?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>[];
}
```

Options of `PoseInertializer`.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { load, sample, seededRng, spring, springState } from "@hackbuild/organic";

// the wasm core is inlined; load() also takes a URL or bytes
await load();

// one seed gives the same motion in Node, in tests and in the browser
const rng = seededRng("rex");
const head = springState(0);
let goal = 0.6;

// 2 seconds at 60 frames per second
for (let frame = 0; frame < 120; frame++) {
  const dt = 1 / 60;
  // about one glance a second, to a random new angle
  if (sample.eventInStep(1, dt, rng)) goal = sample.gauss(rng) * 0.5;
  // critically damped: half way to the goal in 0.12 s, no overshoot
  const yaw = spring(head, goal, 0.12, dt);
  if (frame % 30 === 0) console.log(`frame ${frame}: head yaw ${yaw.toFixed(3)} rad`);
}
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const inert = new PoseInertializer([hips, spine, neck], { positions: [hips] });
// each frame, after you wrote the new pose:
if (switched) inert.capture();
inert.apply(dt, 0.15);
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Calling a wasm class or `PoseInertializer` before `await load()`; the scalar functions are the only part that runs without it.
- Calling `Math.random` for motion. Pass `seededRng(seed)` as the `rng` argument so a seed replays the same motion.
- Passing a stiffness or a frequency where a half life in seconds is wanted.
- Calling `PoseInertializer.capture()` before writing the new pose, or every frame; call it once, on the frame the source changes, then `apply` every frame.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/organic: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (a wasm class or `PoseInertializer` was made before `load()` resolved): `await load()` once at start up
- a `WebAssembly` compile or fetch error (`load(url)` pointed at a missing or wrong file): call `load()` with no argument to use the inlined copy, or check the URL serves `organic_bg.wasm`

---

# @hackbuild/presence

> Make a standing humanoid look present: gaze, blink, breath, idle moves, gestures, a layered clip player and a face driver.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/presence/

## Purpose

- Points the eyes and head at a target with aversion episodes, small saccades, head recruitment past the eye range and clamped eye aim, and tells you when the body should turn.
- Blinks, breathes and schedules idle fidgets, weight shifts and face touches from an injected random source.
- Times pointing, reaching and throwing as weight and angle curves you apply to your own rig.
- Plays clips on a base, body and upper body layer that write every bone, with loop seams and a hand back to idle.
- Drives every expression weight through one face: moods ease in, a quiet face rests at a slight smile, and speech and clip face tracks take their channels.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/presence @hackbuild/organic
```

`@hackbuild/organic` is a dependency and installs with it; the quick start imports `seededRng` from it, so the line names it too. The core entry is plain TypeScript with no wasm and no three.js. `three` is an optional peer used only by the `/three` subpath.

| subpath | needs | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/presence` | nothing beyond `@hackbuild/organic` | none |
| `@hackbuild/presence/three` | `three` (optional peer) | 0.186.1 or later |
| `@hackbuild/presence/iife` | a page with a `THREE` global for the three.js parts | none |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/presence

```ts
function blendPose(a: Pose, b: Pose, w: number, out: Pose, mask?: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>): void
```

out = slerp(a, b, w) per bone, root lerped.

```ts
class Blink {
  constructor(rng: Rng, opts?: BlinkOptions);
  count: number;
  weight: number;
  trigger(): void;
  update(dt: number): number;
}
```

Spontaneous blinks with gaps from 1 to 8 s (median near 3 s, log normal, inferred from published blink studies), 85 percent single, a triangle lid curve that closes in 0.06 s and opens in 0.12 s.

```ts
interface BlinkOptions {
  close?: number;
  maxGap?: number;
  minGap?: number;
  open?: number;
  single?: number;
}
```

Gap, single or double share, and lid timing of spontaneous blinks.

```ts
class Breath {
  constructor(rng: Rng, rate?: number);
  depth: number;
  rate: number;
  update(dt: number): BreathState;
}
```

Breathing at a rate in breaths per minute with an inhale of 40 percent of the cycle and a slower exhale.

```ts
interface BreathState {
  chestPitch: number;
  fill: number;
  phase: number;
  shoulderRise: number;
}
```

One breathing frame: cycle phase, lung fill, chest pitch and shoulder rise.

```ts
function clamp(x: number, lo: number, hi: number): number
```

Clamps a number to the range lo to hi.

```ts
interface Clip {
  bones: number;
  faces?: ClipFace[];
  fps: number;
  frames: number;
  loop: boolean;
  name: string;
  root?: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>;
  rotations: Float32Array;
}
```

A clip on flat arrays: local bone rotations per frame, an optional root track and optional face tracks.

```ts
function clipDuration(c: Clip): number
```

Length of a clip in seconds, from its frame count and rate.

```ts
interface ClipFace {
  name: string;
  weights: Float32Array;
}
```

One expression track of a clip, a weight per frame.

```ts
class ClipPlayer {
  constructor(opts: ClipPlayerOptions);
  readonly bones: number;
  events: PlayerEvent[];
  readonly faces: Map<string, number>;
  readonly pose: Pose;
  layerWeight(layer?: Layer): number;
  loopPlan(c: Clip): LoopPlan;
  play(clip: Clip, opts?: PlayOptions): number;
  release(layer?: Layer, fade?: number): void;
  setLocomotion(speed: number): void;
  stop(layer?: Layer, fade?: number): void;
  update(dt: number): Pose;
}
```

Layered clip player that writes every bone each frame: a base of idle and speed matched locomotion, a body layer and a masked upper body layer, with loop seams and idle handback.

```ts
interface ClipPlayerOptions {
  idle: Clip;
  locomotion?: LocomotionEntry[];
  seam?: SeamOptions;
  upperBones?: readonly number[];
}
```

The idle clip, locomotion loops by speed, the upper body bone set and seam options of a clip player.

```ts
function copyPose(from: Pose, to: Pose): void
```

Copies the rotations and root of one pose into another of the same size.

```ts
function createPose(bones: number): Pose
```

A pose of the given bone count with every rotation at identity and the root at the origin.

```ts

```

Radians per degree.

```ts
function direction(yaw: number, pitch: number): [number, number, number]
```

Unit direction for a yaw and pitch.

```ts
interface ExpressionSink {
  setValue(name: string, weight: number): void;
}
```

What the face writes to: a preset or morph name and a weight.

```ts
class Face {
  constructor(sink: ExpressionSink, opts?: FaceOptions);
  readonly mouth: ExpressionSink;
  blink: boolean;
  lid(weight: number): void;
  set(name: string | null, weight?: number): void;
  setResting(weights: Readonly<Record<string, number>>): void;
  settling(): boolean;
  update(dt: number, clipFaces?: ReadonlyMap<string, number>): void;
  value(name: string): number;
}
```

The face driver: eases moods toward their targets, rests at a slight smile, and writes lid, mouth and clip face weights to one expression sink.

```ts
interface FaceOptions {
  lid?: string;
  rate?: number;
  resting?: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
}
```

Easing rate, resting weights and lid channel name of a face.

```ts
class GazeController {
  constructor(opts: GazeOptions);
  readonly blinker: Blink;
  setMode(mode: GazeMode): void;
  setTarget(p: Vec3 | null): void;
  update(dt: number, eye: Vec3, bodyYaw: number): GazeOutput;
}
```

Where the eyes and head point each frame, with aversion episodes, saccades, head recruitment, clamped eye aim, blinks and a seam hold behind the body.

```ts
type GazeMode = "listen" | "talk" | "think"
```

The conversation state that sets aversion timing: listen, talk or think.

```ts
interface GazeOptions {
  blink?: BlinkOptions;
  eyeOnlyDeg?: number;
  eyePitchDeg?: number;
  eyeYawDeg?: number;
  headHalflife?: number;
  headPitchDown?: number;
  headPitchUp?: number;
  headSlope?: number;
  headYawLimit?: number;
  organic?: boolean;
  rng: Rng;
  seamLimit?: number;
}
```

Random source, eye and head ranges, spring halflife and the organic switch of a gaze controller.

```ts
interface GazeOutput {
  averted: boolean;
  blink: number;
  bodyTurn: number;
  direction: [number, number, number];
  eyePitch: number;
  eyeYaw: number;
  headPitch: number;
  headYaw: number;
  targetYaw: number;
}
```

One gaze frame: head and eye angles, world direction, lid weight, aversion flag and the body turn asked for.

```ts
class HeadLevel {
  constructor(maxLift?: number, halflife?: number);
  halflife: number;
  maxLift: number;
  apply(dt: number, pose: Pose, head: number): number;
  update(dt: number, clipPitch: number): number;
}
```

Head level: mocap idles hold the head 10 to 20 degrees down, which reads as a glare once the eyes aim at a face.

```ts
interface IdleEvent {
  at: number;
  duration: number;
  kind: IdleKind;
  mouth?: boolean;
  shift?: number;
  side: "L" | "R";
}
```

One idle action the scheduler started: a fidget, weight shift or face touch, with its timing and side.

```ts
type IdleKind = "fidget" | "weightShift" | "faceTouch"
```

The kinds of idle action: fidget, weight shift or face touch.

```ts
class IdleScheduler {
  constructor(rng: Rng, changeRate?: number, faceRate?: number);
  changeRate: number;
  faceRate: number;
  update(dt: number, idle: boolean): IdleState;
}
```

Idle scheduler: a postural change about every 20 s, half fidgets, a third weight shifts, the rest easing back to centre (Duarte and Zatsiorsky, vendor), and face touches about 23 an hour (Kwok 2015, vendor).

```ts
interface IdleState {
  active: { event: IdleEvent; weight: number }[];
  shift: number;
  started: IdleEvent[];
}
```

What the idle scheduler started this step, what runs with its weight, and the current weight shift.

```ts
type Layer = "body" | "upper"
```

A clip player layer: the whole body, or the masked upper body.

```ts
interface LocomotionEntry {
  clip: Clip;
  speed: number;
}
```

A locomotion loop and the speed it was recorded at, in meters per second.

```ts

  blend: number;
  restart: number;

}
```

How a loop wraps: the blend window and the time it restarts from.

```ts
function planLoop(c: Clip, opts?: SeamOptions): LoopPlan
```

How a loop wraps: the seam width in degrees, the blend window and the restart time.

```ts
function planReach(distance: number, rng: Rng, hold?: number): ReachPlan
```

A reach plan whose duration grows with distance in the manner of Fitts' law: 0.35 s plus 0.12 s per bit of log2(1 + distance / 0.04) (constants inferred), with a small seeded spread.

```ts
function planThrow(effort: number, rng: Rng): ThrowPlan
```

A throw as a proximal to distal chain.

```ts
interface PlayerEvent {
  layer: Layer;

}
```

A clip player event: a clip started, ended, or handed back to the base layer.

```ts

  background?: boolean;
  fade?: number;

  loopFor?: number;

}
```

Layer, loop, fade, hold, speed and queue policy of one play call.

```ts
const POINT_TIMING: { readonly apex: 1.37; readonly end: 3.3; readonly holdEnd: 2.56; readonly onset: 0.53; readonly retract: 0.6; readonly travel: 0.83 }
```

Pointing timing after Peeters 2013 (vendor): onset 0.53 s, the arm travels for 0.83 s, apex at 1.37 s, hold about 1.2 s.

### @hackbuild/presence/three

```ts
function aimBone(bone: Object3D, child: Object3D, target: Vector3, weight: number): void
```

Turns `bone` in world space so the direction to `child` swings toward `target` by `weight` (0 to 1).

```ts
function applyGaze(g: GazeOutput, rig: GazeRig, neckShare?: number): void
```

Adds a gaze frame onto the rig after the pose is written: head angles are split between neck and head (`neckShare` to the neck), eye angles set the eye bones inside `rig.eyeLimitDeg`.

```ts
function applyPose(pose: Pose, bones: readonly (Object3D<Object3DEventMap> | null)[], root?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap> | null): void
```

Writes a pose onto bones (same order as the clip).

```ts
interface ArmChain {
  hand: Object3D;
  lower: Object3D;
  upper: Object3D;
}
```

The upper arm, forearm and hand bones that `reachArm` swings toward a target.

```ts
function clipFromThree(clip: AnimationClip, bones: readonly string[], opts?: ClipFromThreeOptions): Clip
```

Samples a three.js AnimationClip into a flat Clip over the given bone names.

```ts
interface ClipFromThreeOptions {
  fps?: number;
  loop?: boolean;
  rest?: readonly (Object3D<Object3DEventMap> | null)[];
  rootBone?: string;
}
```

Frame rate, loop flag, root bone and rest rotations for `clipFromThree`.

```ts
const EYE_BONE_LIMIT_DEG: readonly [12, 8]
```

Default eye bone limits of `applyGaze`, degrees (vendor).

```ts
interface GazeRig {
  eyeLimitDeg?: readonly [number, number];
  head: Object3D;
  leftEye?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap> | null;
  neck?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap> | null;
  rightEye?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap> | null;
}
```

The neck, head and eye bones that `applyGaze` writes to, and the eye bone limits.

```ts
function reachArm(arm: ArmChain, target: Vector3, weight: number): void
```

Point or reach: the upper arm, then the forearm, swing toward the target.

```ts
function restStanceFromThree(bones: readonly Object3D<Object3DEventMap>[], names: readonly string[], root?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap> | null): Clip
```

The rest stance over posed bones (same order as `names`) from their current rotations: each arm turn is applied about the body's forward axis in world space, then expressed in the bone's local frame, so rigs whose bones rest in other frames still lower their arms.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { seededRng } from "@hackbuild/organic";
import { ClipPlayer, Face, GazeController, restStance } from "@hackbuild/presence";

// the rest stance as the idle clip: arms down, made in code, no model file
const bones = ["hips", "spine", "head", "leftUpperArm", "rightUpperArm"];
const player = new ClipPlayer({ idle: restStance(bones) });
const gaze = new GazeController({ rng: seededRng("quick") });
const face = new Face({ setValue: (name, weight) => console.log(name, weight.toFixed(2)) });

gaze.setTarget([0.4, 1.6, 1.2]); // a listener's head, meters, +Z forward
face.set("happy", 0.6);
for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) {
  const pose = player.update(1 / 60); // local rotations x y z w per bone
  const g = gaze.update(1 / 60, [0, 1.6, 0], 0);
  face.lid(g.blink);
  face.update(1 / 60, player.faces);
  if (i === 59) console.log(pose.rotations.length, g.headYaw.toFixed(3), g.eyeYaw.toFixed(3));
}
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const wave = player.play(waveClip, { layer: "upper", fade: 0.12 });
player.setLocomotion(1.4); // meters per second picks and blends the locomotion loops
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Writing bones or expression channels from two places. Let `ClipPlayer` own the bones and `Face` own the weights, and add gaze after the pose.
- Calling `Math.random` or passing a fresh seed each frame. Pass one `Rng`, such as `seededRng("name")`, when you build each controller.
- Feeding bones that are not in the normalized humanoid space (+Y up, +Z forward). Load the model through `@hackbuild/avatar` first.
- Forgetting `face.update(dt, player.faces)` each frame: clip face tracks and mood easing only show after it.

---

# @hackbuild/retarget

> Move clips between any rigs through one normalized humanoid space, with readers for BVH, VMD, VPD, VRMA and Unity text clips.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/retarget/

## Purpose

- Defines `HumanoidMotion`, an interchange format of per bone rotations in the normalized space and hip travel in hip heights, so one motion fits a child and a tall adult.
- Maps and measures any skeleton (facing, units, floor, A or T pose) and retargets clips onto and off it with `RetargetRig`.
- Reads BVH, MikuMikuDance VMD and VPD, VRM animation (VRMA) and Unity text clips of transform curves, solving legs keyed only by foot IK.
- Tags a motion by what the body does (wave, squat, nod, spin, walk, dance, idle and more) and packs it into a compact binary form.
- Retargets three.js `AnimationClip`s between scenes, or copies a driver rig's pose onto a target every frame.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/retarget
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/rig` for the bone mapper. three.js is an optional peer, needed only for the `/three` subpath.

| subpath | needs | what |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/retarget` | none | the format, the rig, BVH and VMD parsers, analysis |
| `@hackbuild/retarget/formats` | none | VMD with face tracks, VPD, Unity text clips |
| `@hackbuild/retarget/three` | `three` 0.186.1 or later (optional peer) | scene skeletons, AnimationClip in and out, live retarget, VRMA |
| `@hackbuild/retarget/wasm` | none | the wasm file, to pass to `load()` as a URL |
| `@hackbuild/retarget/inline` | none | the wasm as base64 |
| `@hackbuild/retarget/iife` | `THREE` global for the three parts | single file build, global `HackbuildRetarget`, wasm inlined |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/retarget/formats

```ts
function convertUnityGeneric(c: UnityClip): HumanoidMotion
```

A Unity clip of transform curves (a generic rig) as a humanoid motion.

```ts
interface FaceTrack {
  name: "happy" | "angry" | "sad" | "relaxed" | "surprised" | "aa" | "ih" | "ou" | "ee" | "oh" | "blink" | "blinkLeft" | "blinkRight" | "lookUp" | "lookDown" | "lookLeft" | "lookRight" | "neutral";
  weights: Float32Array;
}
```

One expression's weight per frame, 0 to 1.

```ts
function faceTracks(morphs: { frame: number; name: string; weight: number }[], frames: number): FaceTrack[]
```

VMD morph keys as expression tracks at 30 fps over `frames` frames.

```ts
function isHumanoidClip(c: UnityClip): boolean
```

True when the clip drives a humanoid avatar through muscle curves.

```ts
function isPosingDesktop(text: string): boolean
```

True for a `.vpd` written by a posing tool as JSON (a Unity humanoid pose) rather than MikuMikuDance's text pose.

```ts
interface MotionWithFace {
  faces: FaceTrack[];
  motion: HumanoidMotion;
}
```

A humanoid motion with the expression tracks over the same frames.

```ts
function parseUnityAnim(text: string): UnityClip
```

Reads a Unity `.anim` saved as text (Force Text serialization).

```ts
function parseVpd(bytes: Uint8Array, decode?: (b: Uint8Array) => string): HumanoidMotion
```

A MikuMikuDance pose (`.vpd`, Shift-JIS text) as a one frame motion.

```ts
function readVmd(bytes: Uint8Array, decode?: (b: Uint8Array) => string): MotionWithFace
```

A VMD as a humanoid motion and its face.

```ts
interface UnityClip {
  euler: Map<string, UnityKey[]>;
  float: Map<string, UnityKey[]>;
  name: string;
  position: Map<string, UnityKey[]>;
  rotation: Map<string, UnityKey[]>;
  sampleRate: number;
}
```

The curves of a text serialized Unity AnimationClip.

```ts
interface UnityKey {
  time: number;
  value: number[];
}
```

One key of a Unity curve: time in seconds and its values.

### @hackbuild/retarget

```ts
function analyzeMotion(m: HumanoidMotion): MotionFindings
```

Tags a motion by what the body does: wave, squat, nod, spin, walk, dance, idle and more.

```ts
interface Clip {
  moves: Uint8Array;
  rotations: Float64Array;
  times: Float64Array;
  translations: Float64Array;
}
```

Local rotations and translations per frame.

```ts
function goldenTrace(seed: number): Float64Array
```

A deterministic trace of the core for one seed, compared between the native and wasm builds in tests.

```ts
type HumanBone = typeof HUMAN_BONES[number]
```

One VRM 1.0 humanoid bone name.

```ts
interface HumanoidMotion {
  hips?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>;
  rotations: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Float64Array>>;
  times: Float64Array;
}
```

The interchange format: per humanoid bone, local rotations in the normalized space (identity rest, +Z forward, left on +X), and hip travel in multiples of hip height.

```ts
function load(source?: WasmSource): Promise<void>
```

Loads the wasm core once: from a URL, bytes or a compiled module, or from the inlined copy when you pass nothing.

```ts
function loadSync(source: ArrayBuffer | Module | ArrayBufferView<ArrayBufferLike>): void
```

Loads the wasm core synchronously from bytes or a compiled module.

```ts
interface MotionFindings {
  duration: number;
  energy: number;
  headPitch: number;
  looping: boolean;
  pose: boolean;
  tags: string[];
}
```

What `analyzeMotion` finds in a motion: duration, loop, head pitch, energy and tags.

```ts
function packMotion(m: HumanoidMotion): Uint8Array
```

The compact binary form (`HBM1`, f32, about 16 bytes per bone per frame).

```ts
function parseBvh(text: string): { clip: Clip; skeleton: Skeleton }
```

Parses a BVH file.

```ts
function parseVmd(bytes: Uint8Array, decode?: (b: Uint8Array) => string): VmdMotion
```

Parses a MikuMikuDance VMD file.

```ts
function referenceSkeleton(): Skeleton
```

The 1.70 m reference humanoid as a skeleton with VRM bone names.

```ts
function restFromFirstFrame(skeleton: Skeleton, clip: Clip): { clip: Clip; skeleton: Skeleton } | null
```

When the first frame is the better T pose: that frame as the rest and the clip without it.

```ts
function retargetClip(src: Skeleton, clip: Clip, dst: Skeleton, opts?: { dstUnit?: number; srcUnit?: number }): Clip
```

Retargets `clip` from one skeleton onto another.

```ts
function retargetLimb(srcTop: [number, number, number], srcEnd: [number, number, number], srcLength: number, dstTop: [number, number, number], dstLength: number): [number, number, number]
```

End effector target for a limb of another length.

```ts
class RetargetRig {
  constructor(skeleton: Skeleton, opts?: { unit?: number });
  readonly core: Rig;
  readonly skeleton: Skeleton;
  readonly hipsHeight: number;
  readonly unit: number;
  bind(motion: HumanoidMotion): Clip;
  bones(): ("hips" | "spine" | "chest" | "upperChest" | "neck" | "head" | "leftEye" | "rightEye" | "jaw" | "leftUpperLeg" | "leftLowerLeg" | "leftFoot" | "leftToes" | "rightUpperLeg" | "rightLowerLeg" | "rightFoot" | "rightToes" | "leftShoulder" | "leftUpperArm" | "leftLowerArm" | "leftHand" | "rightShoulder" | "rightUpperArm" | "rightLowerArm" | "rightHand" | "leftThumbMetacarpal" | "leftThumbProximal" | "leftThumbDistal" | "leftIndexProximal" | "leftIndexIntermediate" | "leftIndexDistal" | "leftMiddleProximal" | "leftMiddleIntermediate" | "leftMiddleDistal" | "leftRingProximal" | "leftRingIntermediate" | "leftRingDistal" | "leftLittleProximal" | "leftLittleIntermediate" | "leftLittleDistal" | "rightThumbMetacarpal" | "rightThumbProximal" | "rightThumbDistal" | "rightIndexProximal" | "rightIndexIntermediate" | "rightIndexDistal" | "rightMiddleProximal" | "rightMiddleIntermediate" | "rightMiddleDistal" | "rightRingProximal" | "rightRingIntermediate" | "rightRingDistal" | "rightLittleProximal" | "rightLittleIntermediate" | "rightLittleDistal" | null)[];
  dispose(): void;
  retargetPose(src: RetargetRig, worldR: Float64Array, worldP: Float64Array): { rotations: Float64Array; translations: Float64Array };
  toHumanoid(clip: Clip, opts?: { settle?: boolean; startAtOrigin?: boolean }): HumanoidMotion;
}
```

A mapped and measured skeleton: facing, units, per bone rest alignment.

```ts
function settleOnFloor(m: HumanoidMotion): { motion: HumanoidMotion; shift: number }
```

Settles a motion on the floor; returns the shifted motion and the shift in meters.

```ts
interface Skeleton {
  names: string[];
  parents: Int32Array;
  restR: Float64Array;
  restT: Float64Array;
}
```

Joints with rest transforms; parents come before children.

```ts
function unpackMotion(bytes: Uint8Array): HumanoidMotion | null
```

Reads the compact binary form back into a motion; null when the bytes are not that form.

```ts
interface VmdMotion {
  clip: Clip;
  morphs: { frame: number; name: string; weight: number }[];
  skeleton: Skeleton;
  unit: number;
}
```

A parsed VMD file: its skeleton, its clip, the unit in meters and its morph keys.

```ts
type WasmSource = URL | string | Response | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | WebAssembly.Module
```

Where the wasm core comes from: a URL to fetch, a Response, bytes or a compiled module.

### @hackbuild/retarget/three

```ts
function firstPlayable<M, T>(variants: number, load: (variant: number) => Promise<M>, use: (motion: M) => T | null): Promise<{ bound: T; motion: M; variant: number }>
```

Loads the variants of one clip in order (a pack may ship a pose as vrma, anim and vpd) and returns the first that loads and that `use` accepts; `use` returns null when the motion moves none of the model's bones.

```ts
class LiveRetarget {
  constructor(srcRoot: Object3D, dstRoot: Object3D, opts?: { dstUnit?: number; srcUnit?: number });
  dispose(): void;
  update(): void;
}
```

Copies a driver rig's pose onto a target rig every frame: play any clip library on the driver with its own mixer, call `update()` after it.

```ts
function pickTake<T extends { duration: number; name: string }>(clips: readonly T[], take?: string): T
```

The take to play from a file that holds several (FBX stacks, glTF animations): the one named `take`, else the `mixamo.com` take, else the longest.

```ts
function readVrma(data: ArrayBuffer, fps?: number): Promise<{ faces: FaceTrack[]; motion: HumanoidMotion }>
```

Reads a VRM animation (`.vrma`, glTF with `VRMC_vrm_animation`) as a humanoid motion at `fps`, travel starting at the origin, and its expression tracks (each expression node's X translation is its weight).

```ts
function retargetAnimation(anim: AnimationClip, srcRoot: Object3D, dstRoot: Object3D, opts?: { dstUnit?: number; fps?: number; name?: string; srcUnit?: number }): AnimationClip
```

Retargets an AnimationClip made for `srcRoot` onto `dstRoot`.

```ts
function sampleAnimationClip(anim: AnimationClip, root: Object3D, scene: SceneSkeleton, fps?: number): Clip
```

Samples a three.js AnimationClip on `root` at `fps` into a Clip over `nodes`.

```ts
interface SceneSkeleton {
  nodes: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>[];
  rootParents: Map<number, Matrix4>;
  scales: Float64Array;
  skeleton: Skeleton;
}
```

A skeleton read from a three.js scene graph, with the scene nodes behind each joint.

```ts
function skeletonFromObject3D(root: Object3D): SceneSkeleton
```

The bones under `root` as a skeleton, rest taken from their current local transforms (put the model in its rest pose first).

```ts
function toAnimationClip(clip: Clip, scene: SceneSkeleton, name?: string): AnimationClip
```

A Clip over a scene skeleton as a three.js AnimationClip, tracks bound by node name.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { analyzeMotion, load, packMotion, parseBvh, RetargetRig } from "@hackbuild/retarget";

await load();
// pick any BVH file: its bones map onto the normalized humanoid by name
const input = document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("input"));
input.type = "file";
input.accept = ".bvh";
input.onchange = async () => {
  const file = input.files?.[0];
  if (!file) return;
  const { skeleton, clip } = parseBvh(await file.text());
  const rig = new RetargetRig(skeleton); // meters per unit is guessed from the rest height
  const motion = rig.toHumanoid(clip, { settle: true });
  const found = analyzeMotion(motion);
  console.log(found.duration.toFixed(2), "s,", found.tags.join(" "), packMotion(motion).byteLength, "bytes packed");
  rig.dispose();
};
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { retargetAnimation } from "@hackbuild/retarget/three";

const clip = retargetAnimation(source.animations[0]!, source.scene, avatar.scene);
mixer.clipAction(clip).play();
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Calling a parser or `new RetargetRig()` before `await load()`.
- Retargeting rig to rig directly: read the source into a `HumanoidMotion` with `toHumanoid`, then `bind` it on the target, so any pair of rigs works.
- Passing hip travel in meters: `HumanoidMotion` stores it in hip heights; `bind` scales it to the target.
- Importing `@hackbuild/retarget/three` without three.js installed, or using the single file build on a page without a `THREE` global.
- Forgetting `dispose()` on a `RetargetRig`: it holds wasm memory.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/retarget: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (a parser or rig call before `load()` resolved): `await load()` once first
- `this .vpd is a posing tool pose of unity muscle values, which is not read. save it as a vrma.` (the JSON `.vpd` of a posing tool): export the pose as VRMA
- `not a vpd pose file` (the file does not start with `Vocaloid Pose Data`): check the file
- `this vpd has no bones` (the pose names no bone): check the file
- `not a text unity .anim. save the project with force text serialization.` (a binary Unity clip): set Unity's asset serialization to force text and save again
- `this .anim is a humanoid muscle clip, which is not read. export it from a generic rig or as a vrma.` (a Unity humanoid muscle clip): export from a generic rig or as VRMA
- `no curve in this .anim drives a humanoid bone` (no curve path maps to a humanoid bone): check the clip's bone paths
- `no take named "<take>" in this file` (`pickTake` got a name the file lacks): pick one of the file's take names
- `this file holds no animation. it may be a model, not a motion.` (the file has no clip): load a motion file
- `no VRMC_vrm_animation humanoid in this file. it may be a model, not a vrma.` (`readVrma` got a file without the VRMA extension): load a `.vrma` file
- `this vrma holds no animation` (the VRMA has no clip): check the file

---

# @hackbuild/rig

> Bring any humanoid or legged skeleton into one normalized space: bone name mapping with no per rig table, limb chains, rest pose analysis, and the expression and viseme table.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-motion. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/docs/rig/

## Purpose

- Maps source bone names to the 55 VRM 1.0 humanoid bones by rules (`mapRig`), for Mixamo, VRoid, Unreal, Rigify, 3ds Max Biped, SMPL, MMD and generic names, and reports what is missing, unmapped or ambiguous.
- Finds limb chains on quadrupeds and other rigs (`limbChains`): four legs, tail, ears, spine, neck and head, each with a measured pole.
- Measures a rest pose (`analyzeRest`): which way it faces, its units, its floor, and the rotations that turn it to +Z and lift A pose arms into a T pose.
- Holds one expression and viseme table: the 18 VRM expressions, ARKit 52, the 15 Oculus visemes, morph name aliases and composites, and `resolveExpressions` to bind them to a model's morphs.
- Does the same on three.js objects under `/three`: `mapObject3D`, `chainsOf`, `restOf`, `applyRestFix`.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/rig
```

three.js is an optional peer, needed only for the `/three` subpath.

| subpath | what | needs |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/rig` | mapper, chains, rest analysis, the bone list and the expression table | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/rig/bones` | `HUMAN_BONES` and helpers, with no wasm | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/rig/expressions` | the expression and viseme table, with no wasm | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/rig/three` | `mapObject3D`, `chainsOf`, `restOf`, `applyRestFix` | `three` 0.186.1 or later (optional peer) |
| `@hackbuild/rig/wasm` | the wasm file, for `load(url)` | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/rig/inline` | the wasm as base64, what `load()` uses with no argument | nothing |
| `@hackbuild/rig/iife` | `dist/rig.iife.js`, a classic script setting `HackbuildRig` | `THREE` on the page for the adapter |

ARKit shapes a lip consonant drives on top of the vowel composites, as a share of its viseme weight: closed lips for PP, the lower lip rolled in under the teeth for FF.

```ts
  floor: number;

  units: Units;

```

```ts
  coverage: number;

  dialect: Dialect;
  helpers: number[];
  missingRequired: ("hips" | "spine" | "chest" | "upperChest" | "neck" | "head" | "leftEye" | "rightEye" | "jaw" | "leftUpperLeg" | "leftLowerLeg" | "leftFoot" | "leftToes" | "rightUpperLeg" | "rightLowerLeg" | "rightFoot" | "rightToes" | "leftShoulder" | "leftUpperArm" | "leftLowerArm" | "leftHand" | "rightShoulder" | "rightUpperArm" | "rightLowerArm" | "rightHand" | "leftThumbMetacarpal" | "leftThumbProximal" | "leftThumbDistal" | "leftIndexProximal" | "leftIndexIntermediate" | "leftIndexDistal" | "leftMiddleProximal" | "leftMiddleIntermediate" | "leftMiddleDistal" | "leftRingProximal" | "leftRingIntermediate" | "leftRingDistal" | "leftLittleProximal" | "leftLittleIntermediate" | "leftLittleDistal" | "rightThumbMetacarpal" | "rightThumbProximal" | "rightThumbDistal" | "rightIndexProximal" | "rightIndexIntermediate" | "rightIndexDistal" | "rightMiddleProximal" | "rightMiddleIntermediate" | "rightMiddleDistal" | "rightRingProximal" | "rightRingIntermediate" | "rightRingDistal" | "rightLittleProximal" | "rightLittleIntermediate" | "rightLittleDistal")[];
  unmapped: number[];
}
```

The result of `mapRig`: the humanoid bone of each source node, what is missing or unmapped, the dialect, and the share of required bones found.

```ts
interface RigNodeInput {
  name: string;
  parent: string | number | null;
}
```

A bone of the source skeleton: its name and its parent's index or name.

```ts
type Units = "meters" | "centimeters" | "millimeters" | "unknown" | "decimeters" | "inches"
```

The length unit a rig was authored in, guessed from its height.

```ts
type Vec3 = [number, number, number]
```

A point or direction as `[x, y, z]`, +Y up.

```ts
function wasmBoneNames(): string[]
```

Bone names as the wasm build orders them.

```ts
type WasmSource = URL | string | Response | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | WebAssembly.Module
```

Where the wasm comes from: a URL or path to fetch, a Response, the bytes, or a compiled module.

### @hackbuild/rig/three

```ts
function applyRestFix(root: Object3D, bones: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>, report: RestReport, opts?: RestFixOptions): Group
```

Wraps `root` in a group that faces it +Z, scales it to meters and puts its feet on y = 0, then lifts A pose arms into the T pose.

```ts
function chainsOf(root: Object3D): { chains: LimbChain[]; nodes: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>[] }
```

Limb chains under `root` with poles measured from the current world pose.

```ts
function mapObject3D(root: Object3D): MappedObject
```

Maps the bones under `root`.

```ts
interface MappedObject {
  bones: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>;
  nodes: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>[];
  report: RigMapReport;
}
```

The result of `mapObject3D`: the map report, the scene object of each humanoid bone, and the nodes in report order.

```ts
interface RestFixOptions {
  headHeight?: number;
  straightLegs?: boolean;
  tPoseArms?: boolean;
}
```

Options of `applyRestFix`.

```ts
function restOf(bones: Partial<Record<HumanBone, Object3D>>): RestReport | null
```

Rest analysis of mapped bones at their current world positions.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { analyzeRest, load, mapRig, referenceRest, resolveExpressions } from "@hackbuild/rig";

// the wasm core is inlined; load() also takes a URL or bytes
await load();

// a Mixamo style skeleton as name and parent pairs, as you would read it from a glTF
const names = ["Hips", "Spine", "Spine1", "Spine2", "Neck", "Head", "LeftShoulder", "LeftArm", "LeftForeArm", "LeftHand", "RightShoulder", "RightArm", "RightForeArm", "RightHand", "LeftUpLeg", "LeftLeg", "LeftFoot", "RightUpLeg", "RightLeg", "RightFoot"];
const parent = [-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 6, 7, 8, 3, 10, 11, 12, 0, 14, 15, 0, 17, 18];
const report = mapRig(names.map((n, i) => ({ name: `mixamorig:${n}`, parent: parent[i] ?? null })));
console.log(report.dialect, `coverage ${report.coverage}`, "missing", report.missingRequired, "left forearm is node", report.byBone.leftLowerArm);

// rest pose analysis: facing, units, floor and T pose fixes (here the 1.70 m reference)
const rest = analyzeRest(referenceRest());
console.log(rest?.units, `head at ${rest?.height.toFixed(2)}`, `A pose ${rest?.aPose}`);

// which morphs make each VRM expression on a Ready Player Me style head
const face = resolveExpressions(["viseme_aa", "viseme_O", "eyeBlinkLeft", "eyeBlinkRight", "mouthSmile"]);
console.log(face.aa?.binds, face.blink?.source);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { applyRestFix, mapObject3D, restOf } from "@hackbuild/rig/three";

const { report, bones } = mapObject3D(gltf.scene);
const rest = report.missingRequired.length ? null : restOf(bones);
if (rest) scene.add(applyRestFix(gltf.scene, bones, rest)); // faces +Z, meters, feet on y = 0, T pose arms
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Calling the mapper or rest analysis before `await load()`.
- Treating every rig as a humanoid; check `report.missingRequired` before calling `restOf` or `applyRestFix`.
- Calling `restOf` on a posed model; it reads the current world positions, so measure in the rest pose.
- Keeping your own copy of the expression or viseme table; import it from here so avatar and lipsync agree.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/rig: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (`mapRig`, `limbChains`, `analyzeRest` or an adapter call ran before `load()` resolved): `await load()` once at start up
- a `WebAssembly` compile or fetch error (`load(url)` pointed at a missing or wrong file): call `load()` with no argument to use the inlined copy, or check the URL serves `rig_bg.wasm`
